q42_1_rev: At P.S. 18, the programs in the arts are dedicated to fostering creativity, cultural awareness and individuality in every student. Our goal is to provide opportunities to participate such as student-of-the- month performances, our annual musical, concerts, art family night, various assemblies, ballroom dancing, ballet and cultural celebrations. At P.S. 18, students benefit from ever-evolving, sequential and robust arts programs that use backwards planning and inquiry-based lessons, which adhere to the New York City Department of Education's Blueprints for the Arts curriculum, Common Core standards and Danielson framework.

We have continued our plan to expand arts education in the Shakespeare School. To realize the plans' goals, each teacher incorporates the arts into their day-to-day curriculum. Equitable arts opportunities for students take place daily as the culture of the Shakespeare School continues to be strengthened and supported schoolwide. In order to support this vision, we have identified and developed an art studio, a classroom solely purposed with being the space to provide visual arts instruction from our licensed visual arts teacher. In addition to the day-to-day incorporation of the arts, we also have two Project Arts afterschool programs. One is theater based and the other is visual arts based. We have provided our students with field trips to explore NYC arts. We have included an art gallery exhibit that displays student artwork throughout the school. A classroom teacher is providing a voluntary afterschool program for drumming. We have begun a partnership with Renaissance Youth to provide our fifth grade students with music instruction. Our efforts toward a stronger arts education here at Public School 199 is with the hope to spark policy, future action plans and budget recommendations for implementing a sequential and standards-based curriculum in the arts outlined at EVERY grade level. This process has fostered further community awareness and hopes to provide the structure and catalyst for sustainable relationships between the Shakespeare School and key arts stakeholders.

The arts are vehicles for expression of ideas that serve to enhance educational, academic, and social experiences of children at the school. The arts develop intelligence, competencies, and skills that have a direct link to academic performance and social emotional health. Our goal is to allow students to experience a rich and diverse arts program. Currently, we have a full-time visual arts teacher and a full-time dance teacher providing lessons across all grades. Pre-pandemic, we developed a partnership with Creative Music Programs to ensure our students received music instruction. We hope to continue this partnership next school year. For three years, we have partnered with New Victory Theater, and our students have gone on several field trips and received in school theater workshops. This year students had access to New Victory's virtual curriculum. During this blended school year, we wanted to offer an equitable arts experience for both remote and in-person students. Our STEAM and visual arts programs collaborated to celebrate Lunar New Year. In person students engineered a robotic dragon, and remote students designed its head. Students also designed and printed "dragon dancers" on a 3D printer. Dance and art creations were shared virtually throughout the year making connections to technology and exploring video and sound editing for dance. Two of our core values at PS516 include creativity and resilience. The arts have and will continue to foster these in our students!

Teaching and exposing our students to various arts disciplines at P.S. 135 Sheldon A. Brookner continues to be a strong focus. Providing opportunities for the students to participate in performing arts allows the students to hone their skills. In our dance studio, students learn how to move safely and work collaboratively on dance tasks together. All of our students have an opportunity to showcase their talents through our Holiday and Black History Month assembly programs, monthly performances, talent shows, and multicultural performances for their peers and family members during the school year. Also, the performances provide our entire population with the opportunity to enjoy music, dance, and art. Our dance teacher collaborates with other teachers on their theatrical presentations. We are truly proud of our students.

Students in our visual arts course explore a variety of media, learn new techniques and hone their skills through drawing, printmaking, and collage. Ongoing trips to museums enrich and deepen their study of artists and their process. After the switch to remote learning,  this yearour students worked from home on visual arts projects and created a performing arts production showcasing their talents from their homes that was broadcasted to the entire school community.

At PS 396 the arts program is an integral part of our educational vision. Our goal is to provide an equitable and inspirational arts education for all students that celebrates diversity, teaches tolerance, and prepares students for life in the real world. Conceptual, critical and creative thinking, social skills and cultural awareness are all aspects of performance, music and art-making that are nurtured and encouraged at PS 396. We are a resilient community, and although the global pandemic interrupted our arts residencies, afterschool enrichment programs, and cultural partnerships, we return with an indomitable commitment to engage with students in cultural production that helps them process real world events and their emotional experiences through art making in a place where they feel safe. To this end, the music, visual arts, and theater teachers, along with resident artists and the community, return to their collaboration with classroom teachers to support our inter-disciplinary curriculum and celebrate school events and community success.

Murray Hill Academy has a robust arts program that specializes in both art history and studio art. Our studio art teacher works with students on a variety of highly engaging projects using different art materials such as clay, watercolors, wood, acrylic paint, paper mache, magazines, color pencils and printmaking materials. To supplement our studio arts program, we have been working with Learning through an Expanded Arts Program (LeAp) to bring a professional artist into our school two days a week. We also partner with CITYarts to provide a teaching artist that creates large-scale murals with students in our afterschool art club.   We also work closely with NYC Piano Academy to host an afterschool piano club that culminates in an end-of-year recital at the Liederkranz Foundation. We continue to partner with Hook Arts Media to hire a dance instructor to teach hip hop dance classes and poetry.  We also have an Introduction to Music class that is very popular and a powerful theater class that students really enjoy. We also offer a yoga and meditation class that helps students find balance and peace during their busy day. Additionally, our content teachers are committed to exposing students to the arts and bring our students to many plays, movies, and museums throughout the year, taking advantage of our location in midtown Manhattan. Many of our students take more than the minimum two credits of art. Our goal is continuous exposure to art as a vital part of a well-rounded education.

Due the pandemic the students art experience was very different  this school year.  However, the students still produced some magnificent pieces of art in some of the genres of visual arts. They did not create as much as they normally do.  The ability to just create and design art pieces was like therapy for the students. Giving them time to relax and think about many things and focus on the task at hand.  It was a different art experience for the students. However, overall it was great therapy, social connection with their classmates, and emotional release of anxieties. Hopefully, this will be the year we will be able to expand the arts in our building.

The goal of the P.S. 86 arts program (PreK-6) is based on a commitment to provide our students with the elements of art  allowing them to "live the arts" through an arts-integrated curriculum. The arts are basic to the needs of mankind, aesthetically and socially; however, the uniqueness of the 2020-2021 school year continued to create a "new normal" placing contemporary technology in the forefront of educational objectives. By combining The RULER Approach with a Growth Mindset curriculum and an emphasis on the social emotional substructure needed to balance the technology of distance learning, our arts teachers and classroom teachers recognize and instill the tenets of STEM in correlation with arts and the humanities. P.S. 86 continues to collaborate with New York City's cultural institutions. Our school has worked with The Guggenheim's "Learning Through Art" program since 1997. The students' artwork has been exhibited in the Museum regularly for over 20 years. This year, their artwork will again become part of a virtual exhibition. "Dancing Classrooms". Two 4th grades will complete ten sessions with instructors teaching swing, tango and rhumba online. Our professional music instructors accelerated student work in composition with choral classes singing their own music and poetic lyrics for parents and the P.S.86 community.

The 13K287 arts program is a innovative hybrid opportunity for our students to explore their artistic talents both in-person and remotely. This year we are providing arts education opportunities as follows: received an EASE grant to work with Urban Arts to provide theater arts instruction; afterschool programming in digital music and math; and the P.S. 287 Art Club.

Here at the Locke School of Arts and Engineering we believe it is integral for the students to participate and have experiences that are rich in the arts. We have offered our students a chance to showcase their talents and abilities in our visual arts, music, and dance programs. Through these programs, students learn to use a variety of mediums in visual arts, learn traditional and contemporary songs, play instruments in music, and participate in a dance program based on both dance and physical education standards. These talents are celebrated with the families and the Locke School community in culminating seasonal assemblies throughout the school year. We hope to continue our weekly club period where students can choose from specialized arts classes like band, printmaking, and African dance.  The pandemic has been a challenging time for the arts at the Locke School though students were still able to showcase their work in virtual art exhibits.  They also participate in the yearly Manhattan Borough Arts Festival as we have always done every year.

We currently have music as a full class and CWP working with all 6th graders.  We were able to offer music remotely for all students, and offer the Gibney dance Troupe as part of intro to dance and SEL work for all students and staff. The goal is to create a program that allows for choice and uses arts throughout the curriculum.  NY Edge (our CBO) offers dance after school, as well, for all grades.

We are building on our goals for next year and bringing in a music program for an additional 2 days per week to build on the program to create a chorus and plan for other programs, including technology and music.

We are also using arts in ELA, following the CWP format and investing in art materials.  We will also be working on a school mural of social justice in the field of science.

At Public School 306Q, we believe that a well-rounded education begins with integrating the arts into the curriculum. All students benefit from the opportunity to learn about and experience the arts. Arts education helps bolster a child’s attitude towards school and in turn, makes for a more positive school environment. Next year, we will continue to offer arts education in the classroom and through our cluster program.

PS 169, Sunset Park School is a Title I elementary school with a diverse population of 1214 students. This year we were challenged by the pandemic and forced to restructure our educational programs and shift into remote learning. The arts in particular became a driving force to calm and heal the social-emotional toll that this pandemic took on our students. Through remote dialogue, exposure to art history, encouragement and creativity, we were able to connect and support our students’ emotional and intellectual needs. Our unique arts curriculum offered our students daily exposure to a sequential Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts based visual art, music and drama programs aligned with Common Core State Standards (CCSS). Despite the shutdown of schools and the challenges with Covid-19, students mastered new techniques, engaged in intellectual art conversations and regularly submitted unique artwork to art contests. Some of their many accomplishments are: five exemplary artworks included in the Brooklyn Borough Arts 2021 Virtual Festival; a semi-finalist to the PSART exhibit; eight exemplary artworks included in NYCATA’s “Inside/Outside” exhibit; and five more exemplary artworks in the NYSUT Covid-19 art exhibit. Our own grades 3-5 visual arts exhibit is going to highlight our students’ artistic voices during this unprecedented year. This coming year, through a continued social-emotional approach and hands-on art-making in the classroom, we are eager to continue to support our emerging artists and foster their appreciation for the arts.

We currently have school-day sequences for music, visual arts and dance for grades six through twelve. We prioritize access for all learners, and we emphasize performance at venues throughout the city (not this year because of COVID).   Our music program is currently focused on ensemble playing. Since most of the students are remote this year, our Esperanza Band has not had any performances.  Students are practicing individually, some in the building and others at home.  Students learn music theory and composition as well as performance technique under the direction of a Grammy Award winner/teacher. Our visual arts program is a grade six through twelve sequence focused on developing the fundamentals and exploration of the visual arts and developing scholar talent under the instruction of an award winning art teacher.  We offer afterschool sewing club for 6th graders in which they learn to use sewing machines. We offer studio art  for high school students that is currently dedicated to painting a mural in one of the school’s common areas.  Students who are interested can stay afterschool for diverse art-related activities provided by Union Settlement Community Learning Center.

In the Visual Art classes, our Instructor has designed each trimester in the following ways:
1st Trimester: students focus on learning art vocabulary including learning the Elements and Principles of Art. They demonstrate their knowledge through the creation and discussion of abstract art. Students create an abstract word design demonstrating their knowledge of the Elements of Design; line, color, shape, value, texture, form, and space.
2nd Trimester: students focus on developing their observational drawing skills. They learn about the perception of edges, contour drawing, the perception of space, negative and positive space drawing, the perception of light on form, drawing simple objects with directional light, and they study proportion and perspective through 1-point and 2-point perspective drawing. Students create abstract designs demonstrating their knowledge of the Principles of Design:  Balance, emphasis, contrast, movement, variety, unity, and rhythm.
In the 3rd trimester students focus on a project that encompasses and culminates learning over the year. They formally analyze artwork with historical references in mind, and review employment possibilities in the arts. Students create a symbolic self-portrait demonstrating their knowledge of symbolism, portraiture, composition, and observational drawing which includes, understanding proportion and the perception of edges, space, and light on form.   (See below for our Dance Program description).

At Cambria Heights Academy we believe in offering all our students multiple opportunities to engage in the arts. We offer a rigorous graphic design sequence where participating students are able to earn 3 credits from SUNY Farmingdale. Most of our course offerings are digital, such as, music production, film production, and photography. We also offer chorus, intro to music, and drawing electives.

At Public School 443, The Family School, we believe that art affords students unique ways of knowing and expressing what they know. Through art, students extend their aesthetic awareness and judgement by making art that communicates their ideas, perceptions, and feelings. Learning experiences in art enable learners to understand the role of art throughout history and in their own society. Art experiences help students to develop: • an enriched appreciation for works of art through time and culture • the ability to respond to others’ artwork with sensitivity and respect • a heightened awareness of the role art has in lifelong learning • confidence in themselves as makers of art with the potential for using their abilities in future art-related and other careers At our school, students have access to two full-time art teachers: music and the visual arts. Our students work with professional visual artists bringing their passion, creativity, knowledge, and skill to the classroom, guiding students to discover and develop their own creative expressions.

For the 2020-2021 school year, P.S. 225 The Eileen E. Zaglin had one visual arts teacher who provided instruction remotely. The classroom teachers provided opportunities for students to develop their artistic skills. Our parents participated in arts activities remotely with two of our visual arts teachers.

Our school continues to participate in the arts partnership between District 29 and the Guggenheim Museum. Through this partnership, professional development is provided to the school's social studies teachers. A teaching artist has also visited the school to further support the social studies teachers.  In addition, our school started a 9-week arts residency with Arts Horizons this year.  One in-person teaching artist worked with our in-person students.  Two remote teaching artists worked with our remote students.

Like many schools across the city, we have experienced a tremendous disruption to our traditional arts program due the pandemic. However, we adjusted the program online. We continued to offer arts learning through our collaboration with an arts  to community based organization to provide arts integration with four classes. We also provided opportunities for students in art class to showcase their work in virtual galleries.

Fordham High School for the Arts is an arts-focused high school with a 4 year sequence in 6 majors: Dance, Drama, Instrumental/Music Production, Technical Theater, Visual Art and Vocal Music. FHSA offers comprehensive arts and academic curriculum which culminates in an Advanced Regents diploma, college acceptance, and career readiness. Numerous partnerships include Roundabout Theatre Company, Metropolitan Opera, Carnegie Hall, Lincoln Center Theatre, Studio in a School. 
Guest artist visits afford students the opportunity to explore and develop their talents in various mediums of artistic expression. Work-Based Learning Internships allow students an opportunity to explore career paths in the arts and beyond.

In school year 2020-21, Alvin Ailey Dance Theater returned to CMSP 328 to offer musical theater and hip hop dance workshops. Our goals for the 2021-22 school year are to build integration of arts into our core academic subjects as well as strengthen our primary arts partnerships. In addition, we will work to build rigor in our arts programming by developing more comprehensive arts assessments. Finally, we will work to increase the number of arts experiences made available to our students and their families. These goals will become increasingly important as we return to an in-person learning environment.

Samuel Huntington Elementary’s ARTS program consists of experiences in dance, music, theater, and visual arts focused on detecting and responding to the social injustices of the world they are growing up in. Scholars are encouraged to utilize the ARTS to speak out against social injustice and fight to create social justice within their school and community. At Samuel Huntington Elementary school, we provide scholars with integrated ARTS opportunities to enrich academic experiences. Our elementary scholar’s art classes seek to foster interest.Our elementary art classes include basic drawing, painting and crafts. Our music curriculum consists of three strands: Listening and Responding, Performing, and Composing.Our grade 5 scholars participate in  composing music digitally with the use of Soundnation. Our dance curriculum allows students to explore the elements of dance through observation and performance. Scholars learn tap, ballet, jazz,  African, and hip hop dance throughout the year. Our theater curriculum is designed to allow our scholars to explore a variety of activities appropriate to their age level, including role play, charades, acting out scenes and improvising skits. At Samuel Huntington Elementary, we encourage students to achieve three primary goals in the ARTS. We wish to create social and emotional awareness within our sccial and emotional awareness within our scholars. We strive for scholars to develop empathy and to understand their own feelings.

We provide a four-year program in art that explores fine art techniques along with art history and the application of these skills in various art-related industries. All our students study the business of the arts and learn both digital and darkroom photography techniques. Students create portfolios over their four-year experience and write artists' statements and related essays. We aim to provide as varied a program as possible in the many subjects in the arts, including design, illustration, gallery and curatorial techniques. Our close connection with the business, industry and post-secondary education communities ensures that the standards, knowledge and expectations are continually updated and reassessed. This connection also allows students to have access to special enrichment, and unique internship and on-the-job training opportunities.

At PS/IS 163, fostering our students’ creativity and talent is a major part of our educational mission and is a major component of our students' education. Our rich arts program includes classes in visual arts, dance, music, and theater. 

Our visual arts program provides students in grades K-8 a well-rounded visual arts experience that covers both art history and hands-on art projects. Our dance program exposes students to various types of dance, classical and contemporary, and presents them with the opportunity to express themselves through movement. In addition to regularly scheduled music classes, our school has a chorus, a guitar club, and an orchestra. The students who are members of these groups, as well as many others, perform in our winter concert and our spring arts festival. Our theater program educates students on classical theater, as well as modern. Students work on projects, plays, review writing, and technical theater. 

At PS/IS 163, the arts are an integral part of student learning, as they help students to make cross-curricular connections and give them a sense of pride and accomplishment by recognizing their creative talents and potential.

At P.S. 204 Vince Lombardi, we have always focused on engaging our students in all aspects of the arts, including visual arts, dance, theater, and music.  In a typical school year, students in K-5 have the opportunity to broaden their skills in our visual arts program, where our arts teachers utilize The Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. Our teachers engage students in various visual arts projects providing them ongoing opportunities to partake in self and peer assessment aligned to the standards. We have two full-time certified music teachers who, in a typical school year, provide music instruction to students in grades K-5. In prior years, our kindergarten students perform in an annual gift sharing musical performance. Our 3rd graders learn the recorder. Our 4th graders study various Broadway musicals (Inside Broadway) and perform acts from each of them. Our 5th grade students have an opportunity to play in our school band, and/or join our school's chorus and perform at various concerts. In a typical year, all students in grades Pre-K through 5 learn different styles of dance and perform in a schoolwide dance festival held annually each spring, and our fifth grade students receive instruction by Dancing Classrooms in various styles of ballroom dancing. Finally, our English language learners have the opportunity to engage in the TheatreMoves program, where they focus on collaboration and communication culminating in a theatrical performance.

Public School 96, The Richard Rodgers School, is a diverse school community committed to creating an equitable educational environment of excellence for all participants. We serve scholars in grades PK -5, and our goal is to have all of our students take an active role in their arts education through hands-on activities and explorations. PS 96 offers arts education in the fields of visual arts, music, dance and theater through granted programs, programs through cultural organizations, and in class instruction. We are proud of the programs that are available to our students, including drumming, acting through Stella Adler, story telling, and dance. Our students receive weekly visual arts and music education. Many are able to take part in an abundance of afterschool arts programs, including Little Orchestra, Wolf's Den Arts and Crafts, and  a variety of programs through the 21st Century Leadership Grant in dancing, theater, and music. Parents and families are connected to their students' arts education through our interactive online art gallery featured on artsonia.com as well as through the Google Classroom platform.  Due to the unique circumstances of this year, the arts program has adapted so that every student, learning remotely or in person, has the opportunity to receive a quality arts education.  Both the music and visual arts teachers created arts lessons via video and over Zoom for remote learners while teaching in person learners in their classrooms.
We have a full-time visual arts teacher who is implementing a visual arts curriculum with our ninth grade students.

At Newtown High School our students prepare portfolios for college and career readiness in the arts. Students are familiar with the NYS Standards and NYC Blueprints for the Arts. Scholars are exposed to various art forms, tools and techniques to produce artworks and perform, and they develop observational skills and how to develop and discuss an opinion when comparing and contrasting their artwork and the work of others. Students are introduced to professions in the arts and are encouraged to develop their goals towards artistic careers. This year we offered Advanced Placement Art in 2D. This year with remote learning, we were still able to have students work accepted and exhibited at the Metropolitan Museum PS Art and the Queens Borough Festival for Music and Visual Arts.
Meyer Levin School for the Performing Arts offers comprehensive arts education in the following subject areas: instrumental band, steel band, chorus, dance, theater and visual arts.

PS 103 provides instruction in music.  There are two music teachers at the school, one of whom works for the NYCDOE and holds NY State licensure, and one who is employed by the non-profit educational organization, Education Through Music. Every student is provided with general music instruction. There is a chorus program for students in grades 3-5 and a band program for students in grade 5. Ensembles did not take place during the 2020-21 school year due to the pandemic, but will resume in Fall 2021. Students have ample musical performance opportunities both in the school and in the greater community. The chorus performed in the Chrysler Building and World Trade Center in December 2019 and also performed in community nursing homes. PS 103 holds annual winter and spring concerts in which all students participate, and three to four separate concerts for the ensembles. The school annually partners with Jazz at Lincoln Center and hosts jazz musicians to perform educational concerts for students. In 2020, a group of students attended a New York Youth Symphony concert at Carnegie Hall. Throughout remote learning, the music department held four virtual meetings per week with students and sustained high participation. During remote learning, students were able to create, perform, and respond musically through virtual assignments and collaborative projects.

We believe art promotes rigorous content learning and academic achievement in all disciplines. The arts at P.S. 112 Lefferts Park benefit and meet the needs of all diverse learners. Students in our school receive weekly instruction in both art and music. We strive to provide a sequential learning experience that builds a strong foundation. Prior to the onset of the pandemic, students engaged in learning across all strands of the Blueprints for the Arts. P.S. 112 supported the arts through strong visual arts, music, and dance programs. We had many collaborations with arts organizations that provided students with additional exposure and experiences in the all the arts, including theater. We look forward to resuming our arts education programs and collaborations in the 2021-2022 school year.

The art program at the High School for Law and Public Service seeks to provide all students with the time, space and support to learn what it means to be an artist. We embrace a vision of art education as an integral part of a student's core education. We therefore provide students with rich opportunities to express themselves artistically through a variety of media or performances, to explore career opportunities available in the art world, to learn about art history and the role that art plays in cultures throughout the world, and to develop an understanding of how art is related to all forms of expression and is connected to other subjects of study. We offer a studio visual arts and a theater course as well as a competitive improvisational theater team. We also provide arts engagement in several robust afterschool clubs including spoken word, theater, vocal and media arts.

PS46K is a STEAM school with the arts-infused throughout the curriculum, providing opportunities for differentiated instruction within various learning modalities. The arts inform and energize our project-based learning model; supporting and reinforcing learning while developing skills and understandings in individual arts disciplines. 
While the school went through the last year with hybrid learning and other challenges we found our students met the test with flexible thinking and creative problem-solving that has been instilled in them through our curriculum.
Families enthusiastically engaged in the arts programming during the past year. Students with families attended virtual concerts and field trips.  All arts programming was family-focused.
Grade-appropriate lessons are designed to enhance vocabulary and critical thinking skills necessary to prepare students for college and beyond. In addition to an experiential curriculum, students demonstrate mastery of concepts and content as well as processes. We utilize the rich cultural resources of New York City as an extension of classroom activities.
Due to the current remote learning for 2020-2021, PS 583, students participated in virtual opportunities by visiting museums and taking part in art activities through classroom instruction.

At P.S. 68 Cambridge, we strive to educate the whole child. Our goal is to equip our students with the ability to express themselves through art, to enhance their lives by the arts, and to gain a valuable appreciation of the arts as a vital component of their education.  We brought outside virtual experiences  into our school and used volunteers with kindergarten to create a digital performance.    We implemented a virtual annual holiday musical event alongside our annual dance festival. We  maintained our partnership with Studio in a School, which culminates in a school-wide visual arts exhibit and celebration. We had the opportunity to work with ArtsConnection again in afterschool virtual dance classes.. PTA increased our arts with recorded monthly art projects that were shared with our school community.  We hope to partner again with PTA and Greater Ridgewood Youth Council to include in-person programs and seasonal schoolwide events which include visual arts experiences, as well as music and dance opportunities next year.

All students take a visual arts elective in grade 9 and a two credit visual arts course in grade 10 exploring a variety of media through collage, drawing, painting and mural design. They study contemporary artists and explore the issues of identity and self. Students have the option to apply for Advanced Art in eleventh and twelfth grade, where they develop a portfolio for post-secondary arts programs. In partnership with Manhattan Class Company, students explore drama integrated into all English classes, from grades nine through twelve, with reinterpretations of Shakespeare, spoken word poetry, dramatic interpretation of American novels, and rhetoric. There is also an afterschool drama program, which culminates in our annual school play. Our afterschool program offers rock music club and dance club.

We partner with Bronx Arts Ensemble, and they provide theater, dance, and visual arts for our scholars. We also partner with AOC who provide percussion for our scholars. We partner with elite drumming to provide drumming instruction for the scholars as well.

P.S. 105 The Blythebourne has a strong commitment to arts education and recognizes it’s potential to enrich every aspect of teaching and learning. Our goals, strategies, and major initiatives center on supplying all of the student population with instruction in visual arts, music, dance, and theater, using the New York City Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts, which are aligned to the Common Core State Standards. All students actively engage in the processes that constitute creation, performance, and participation in the arts. They respond to and analyze the arts with an understanding of the cultural dimensions and contributions of all arts disciplines. The arts instruction is implemented using a comprehensive and sequential standards-based approach, targeting the benchmarks in the blueprints. This allows students to be art makers, have literacy in the arts, make connections, be aware of community and cultural resources and develop into lifelong learners of the arts.

All new incoming students participate in a Introduction to Theater course, where they learn the craft of all three of our art major options. In their Sophomore year students at School for Classics have the opportunity to choose one of three art majors at our school. These include stage craft, which includes building the sets for our school performances and learning the craft of theater behind the scenes, actin,; where students learn the skills of performance in small acts and larger theater productions, or visual arts, where students learn the skills and techniques needed to build their art portfolio

Despite the pandemic related challenges, we preserved most of our arts programs and engaged our entire school community through a culturally responsive arts curriculum, addressing individuality, cultural identity, as well as social-emotional awareness & wellness.  We maintained strong partnerships with Arts Connection, Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rubin Museum of Art, Midori & Friends, and New Victory Theater to provide arts opportunities and instruction to our students. We also ran a visual arts club for grades 3-5 and participated in several visual art contests and community art related fairs.  Our students’ artwork was showcased by the New York State Senate twice this year.  In addition, we had several winners in the Queens Arts Festival 2021, PS ART 2021, and the 2021 NYSATA Legislative Art Exhibit.  To additionally benefit our school community, we offered weekly recorded livestream instruction in visual arts, music and dance throughout the year.   This year we renewed our strong partnership with Carnegie Hall and three programs:  Ensemble Connect (residency with a professional musician); Musical Explorers (multicultural music study and virtual concert for K-2); and Music Educators Workshop (professional development program for music teachers).  We ran two remote guitar groups for 3rd grade students and their families where students learned guitar and wrote songs.  Finally, remote grades 3-5 students learned to express themselves by composing songs in Soundtrap.

The arts program at Mott Haven Village Preparatory High School includes visual arts. Visual arts incorporates the study of movements in art history, famous artists from those movements, the Elements of Art, and Principles of Design. Throughout the units of study, students complete writing assignments, interpret and analyze artwork, participate in gallery walk activities, engage in peer and self critiques. Our students produce work in areas such as, but not limited to, drawing, painting, and sculpture.

P.S. 376 is a PK-3 multi-disciplinary curriculum school (adding on a new grade level every year until grade 5), which embeds the arts in diverse ways. Our Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Math (STEAM)  Project Based Learning (PBL) projects integrate the arts utilizing recycled materials and utilizing the NYC Blueprints for the Arts. Additionally, our centers in the classroom routinely provide opportunities for our students to express themselves in all the arts including theater. We are continuously looking to find a cultural arts organization which we can forge a partnership that will provide us support with our school's mission and vision. We were able to incorporate Virtual Recess this year for all of our remote students twice a week where most activities were arts-aligned.

Throughout the challenges of the pandemic during School year 2020-21, Public School 184Q was still able to engage our students with arts education that included visual arts, music, and dance. All students in grades K-5 received weekly instruction in visual arts. Students in grades Prek-5 received weekly music instruction. All students in grades Prek-5 received a late spring residency in dance through City Center.  The art, music, and dance instruction was tied to content area learning, thus reinforcing academic knowledge; it enhanced both fine and gross motor skills and coordination, built a sense of confidence and a chance to shine outside of academics as well as providing students with knowledge specific to the art form.

I.S. 211 John Wilson School provides visual arts to the students.  Emphasis is placed on understanding the elements of art and principles of design as a composition.  Students explore a variety of artists, art processes and materials such as drawing, painting and two and three dimensional design.
The arts at P.S. 288 The Shirley Tanyhill were interrupted this school year due to the pandemic and programming.

Despite the Covid 19 pandemic, the arts continue to be an essential element of education, just like reading, writing, and mathematics, music, dance, visual arts, and theater are all keys that unlock profound human understanding and accomplishment. Students in grades 3K through grade five receive a broad range of instruction in the arts. From a fusion of opera and visual arts with Time-In Art to piano lessons sponsored by Keys of Inspiration to Dancing with Yaffa and the American Ballet Theater, students have a broad range of art engagement. Our own music teacher provides piano lessons teaching the students how to read music notes and produce their own pieces. Students receive direct instruction in the visual arts each week: interpreting the work of others, as well as creating their own works of art with an emphasis on technique. Students have had the opportunity to virtually attend various art galas, operas, and culturally themed events in many of New York City's esteemed museums. For the 2021-22 school year, we will continue to provide high quality arts experiences for our students.

Public School 169Q is dedicated to creating a nurturing and intellectually enriched environment that develops each child's unique capabilities. The arts can be used as a vehicle to foster creativity as well as parent and community involvement. Our dedication is evident by the presence of a full-time music and part-time visual arts teacher, a dedicated music room, and our partnership with arts organizations. All students in grades K through fifth grade create visual art, which is exhibited throughout our school and at our annual art show. As a school-wide enrichment school, all students in Grades 1 through 5 are given an opportunity to choose areas of interest to study weekly.

The Bronx High School of Science (BHSS) adds a great deal to our STEM education focus with several opportunities for our students to explore the arts. It is our mission to provide our students with opportunities for interdisciplinary experiences that combine the unique mix of fine arts, visual arts, music and drama. Our students have a regular opportunity to perform in school and outside of school. At BHSS, we have a high-caliber winter concert featuring our concert band, jazz band, chorus and orchestra. These groups were unable to perform live this year due to Covid 19.  S!NG gave a smashing performance of hysterical spoofs written and performed by its many student members - virtually this year. Our students have participated in our annual mask creation contest and were winners in many photography contests. Editors and contributors are busy designing Dynamo and Vox Discipulorum, our literary/world language magazines that includes a great amount of student artwork along with poetry and prose. Many of our artists have been recognized in myriad contests around the city. Our art history students will take the Advanced Placement exam soon. We have enjoyed dance performances by NASHA and LUNAR, student clubs in our school that perform annually. Our students create a weekly television program "Wolverine TV" and this production continued through remote learning. Students and teachers contributed performances for a virtual show!

At PS 56, we have a full-time dance instruction that sees all students in the school, Pre-K through 5th grade.  In the dance program, the dance teacher teaches a variety of dance styles and genres and culminates each program with a performance in the winter and spring.  For visual arts, we partner with Studio in a School to provide visual arts experiences to all students.  We utilize residencies so children engage in visual arts for approximately five to six months of the school year weekly.  For music, we partner with Little Orchestra Society which also provides a residency for five to six months out of the school year.

The arts program was decimated due to the COVID-19 pandemic. With remote, blended, and in-person learning rotating throughout the year, combined with scheduling set forth by the central NYCDOE eliminating prep periods, it was impossible to conduct an arts program this year.

Consistent with the standards of the International Baccalaureate organization, we offer a robust arts program that offers courses in visual arts, graphic design, theater, culinary arts, and dance in grades 6-12.

Members of the Public School 253Q community believe in the benefits and need for arts education as part of our students instructional development. We offer classes in visual arts as well as dance as part of their instructional program, and we look forward to receiving grants to further implement art into the lives of our students. This year we participated in a New York City Ballet Residency program for ballet. Additionally, we have been partnering with Loveessense over the last several years, including songwriting to two classes this year. As we move forward, we are always looking to bring more arts education into the lives of our students.

The Crispus Attucks Young, Gifted and Talented Arts Studio is dedicated to developing observation skills, technical ability, and creating finished artwork to encourage self-confidence, knowledge, and enthusiasm. Our program is designed to enrich students through the visual and performance arts. The arts curriculum is directly aligned with the Common Core Learning Standards for visual and performance arts. Our goal for this year was to spark students’ thinking, creativity, and leadership skills by providing a comprehensive and engaging program. Due to the Coronavirus pandemic, students were introduced to the arts through remote learning. Students were inspired by this new way of learning which enabled exposure to virtual field trips, including museums, zoo's and cultural arts centers around the country and the world. This use of innovative teaching practices in virtual classrooms included art tutorials, games, and interactive visuals. It allowed the students to enhance creativity using a variety of mediums and differentiated learning styles. Students were encouraged to use technology as well as everyday items found around the house creating a variety of artworks that express a new form of artistry.

At P.S. 88 Seneca, we have implemented a rich music experience that all students have access to, whether in person or remote. Our licensed music teacher has secured multiple grants to provide instruments such as guitars, bucket drums, ukeleles, keyboards, and drums to name a few.  Students are learning about creating digital music through a software program.  We have also partnered with a fellow District 24 school (PS 89Q) for a combined glee club. We have incorporated visual arts in the classrooms through the classroom teacher, as well as a Saturday academy with Creative Art Works.

At P.S. 12 James B. Colgate, we believe that our role as a school should go beyond teaching the core subjects and that we must emphasize the importance of the arts in the development of every student. Arts education and engagement are embedded into our school’s curriculum throughout every grade and content area. During the 2020-21 school year, all first and second grade students participated in a mini Together in Dance residency incorporating social and emotional learning into dance. Through this residency students’ emotional learning was incorporated into creative movement. Materials For The Arts provided virtual meets where students had the excitement of class trips through hands-on visual arts classes. Teachers incorporate the arts into their social studies and science curriculum to offer our students the opportunity to appreciate our world from different perspectives. Our school embeds culturally responsive education through our arts programs. At P.S. 12, we are committed to celebrating our diverse student population through the arts.

Health, Education, and Research Occupations High School (HERO) offers students a comprehensive range of arts electives: visual arts, theater, film studies, and dance, which incorporate the NYS Learning Standards for the Arts as well as supports the socio-emotional growth of our students. Afterschool programs include a visual arts club, drama club, and the cypher hip hop and spoken word club. Ninth grade students wrote and performed an original play at the NYC Student Shakespeare Festival. This endeavor was supported by the Creative Arts Team (CAT) afterschool workshop and comprised of ninth and tenth grade students who met twice a week at HERO.  During the 2020-21 school year, students have participated in virtual dance performances and their artwork displayed in online portfolios.

KAPPA V Knowledge and Power Preparatory Academy recognizes that each child is an individual, that all children are creative and all children have the ability to succeed. Success can come in the form of academics and artistic talents. Because of this, we strive to expose our students to various arts disciplines: when the arts are incorporated into every discipline students demonstrate a better understanding of the curriculum. Our students are exposed to visual arts, photography, various forms of dance, musical theater and steel pan. Our goal is to tap into the hidden talents of our students, while creating the best version of themselves.

The vision of the Robert H. Goddard Middle School Arts program remains dedicated to providing students with a comprehensive education with a particular emphasis on the arts. This includes Band, Chorus, Computer & Visual Arts and its connection to SEL (social emotional learning) by accessing the ability to view the world through a holistic lens and be well prepared to embrace the various challenges of crisis, such as COVID, college & career readiness, as intrinsically motivated, socially conscious, and inspired individuals. The goal will be accomplished by strengthening core instruction, knowing each student well, and providing a shared and inclusive curriculum, through blended learning platforms, a professional development plan, strong family ties, and culturally responsive sustaining education. These shared priorities are cultivated with our stakeholders participation in this school community, supporting and encouraging each student's ability to demonstrate independence, building strong content knowledge and understanding other cultures and perspectives. Creative Connections provided New York Pops, and we are embarking on a partnership with Midori & Friends for this years end for extended programs.

The Fine and Performing Arts Program (FPA) at I.S. 5 The Walter Crowley Intermediate School engages students in work that embraces creative and culturally responsive means for expression and individuality, critical thinking, and an empowered student voice in an environment that supports innovation and inspiration. Our school offers arts education in all of the four arts: dance, drama, music, and visual arts. We offer a tech course that routinely integrates film/documentary work. We are also slated to receive a full upgrade of our onsite TV studio through capital funding and look forward to outlining its use as part of FPA studies in the coming years. The FPA Department allows all of our students the ability to experience the arts. Our teachers make social emotional and art-centered connections with our students. In the coming year, as we learn further about requirements for art study, we will be looking for innovative solutions in partnerships, and branching out to include opportunities for our families to enjoy as well.

P.S. 386 has a great art program where students are taught to understand the Elements of Art and Principles of Design as a basis for composition. Students explore a variety of artists, art processes and materials such as drawing, painting, printmaking, two & three-dimensional design, and sculpture.

Students are introduced to art history and learn to appreciate different art forms through viewing original works of art and use of the Smartboard technology. Art projects are often designed to complement the classroom curriculum.

Currently, Public School 111 has a full-time music teacher and visual arts teacher for grades Pre-K through five. Due to the restrictions of COVID, our normal arts partnerships were cancelled for the 2020-2021 school year.  Orchestra of St. Luke’s is an afterschool program servicing about 35 students in grades one through five. It continued to provide music lessons separate from the school setting via ZOOM for families that were interested.  Our goal is to have a grade specific arts program for each grade provided by outside cultural arts organizations in addition to our full-time music and visual arts teachers.

We offer arts classes for students at every grade level, including instrumental music, music production, drama, and media arts. Performance opportunities include two annual showcase concerts that are collaborative productions by students and staff.

Queens Academy High School offers a range of studio-based visual arts courses that include mixed media, drawing, painting, and printmaking. In these courses, students are able to develop their ability to experiment and the confidence to tap into their own creativity. They expand their imaginative capacities while experiencing a variety of art media. Within each art medium, they develop the skills, knowledge, and appreciation needed to best express their artistic selves.  In these courses, students learn to effectively use the language of the Elements of Art and the Principles of Design, and the terminology associated with their growing knowledge of tools, materials, and techniques. Students use the rich vocabulary of visual arts as they analyze, discuss, and assess their own artwork and that of their peers. Students reflect on and write about their art making process, and read and write about a broad range of artists related to that process.  Additionally, we offer Art History courses that are designed to give students the opportunity to discover, appreciate, and acquire knowledge of art history through the ages. The course involves critical thinking and students learn to examine and analyze forms of artistic expression from diverse cultures and understand their contributions to the arts.  Students develop their understanding of art within social, cultural, and historical contexts. They come to understand how art may be used to help them observe and interpret their ever-expanding world.
Students are engaged in a variety of art explorations, including the visual arts, music, dance and movement.  We have  partnerships with Harmony, Project, ASPIRA of New York and Bronx Arts Ensemble.

Our school's arts program consists of music, visual arts and dance. We have had dance for four years, visual arts for three years and music for one year. Previous to this we had Reader's Theater. Our program is very necessary for the children we serve. They come from a low income neighborhood and are not exposed to very much. Through our arts program, they have access to a plethora of ways to express themselves through the arts. We plan to continue next year with dance, music, and visual arts.

John Bowne High School is proud of our Bowne Visual Arts Institute.  Students in this institute can select a sequence in either the two-dimensional track or three-dimensional track. Courses in the 3D track include: Studio Art, 3D Design and Sculpture, and Sculpture 2 and Ceramics. Courses in the 2D track include: Studio Art, Drawing and Painting, and Printmaking and Graphics. Portfolio, Advanced Placement Art and Design and Art History are included in the senior year in both tracks. These visual arts sequences will culminate in the NYC Department of Education commencement exam in the visual arts and successful completion of the sequence will result in a Chancellor's Endorsed Diploma in the Arts.  We look forward to the next school year, 2021-22, when the Bowne Visual Arts Institute will be an ed-opt program.  John Bowne offers a music major with a concentration in chorus, band, and orchestra. Each concentration includes a junior and concert level course. Additional music courses include Music Experience, Piano, Guitar, and Percussion. John Bowne also offers an Academy for Creative Artists (ACA) program.  Our goal is to provide an enriched artistry program through a sequence of highly varied writing and performance courses both in-person and remotely. Through writing, workshopping, performances and literary experiences, students will be prepared for the rigors of professional work in both the writing and dramatic arts arenas, as well as in college and beyond.

Academy for College Preparation and Career Exploration: A College Board School utilizes Puppetry in Practice, an organization that is committed to using the arts as a lens through which students experience, learn from and appreciate the world’s rich history of ideas, cultures and imagination. Established in 1979, Puppetry in Practice is an independent, not-for-profit organization housed in the School of Education at Brooklyn College. Puppetry in Practice assembles artists from around the world and places them in New York City schools and other educational environments to provide hands-on, arts-based approaches to language development and written, oral and visual expression. It also uses the creative arts to enhance literacy, spark curiosity and imagination, and engage in cultural immersions in the countries of origin that make our city great. Puppetry in Practice introduces and instills an enthusiasm for the creative spirit in every individual, at any age, through various means of expression. Through the power of storytelling, using centuries-old art forms or new electronic media, Puppetry in Practice encourages exploration by partnering with schools in building communities, both internally and externally. We believe the world’s great stories bridge cultures and help young people become aware of their creative selves, the contributions of others and their connections to a global community.

q40_r1_c1_3: Cumbe: Center for African and Diaspora Dance
q42_1_rev: The focus of the arts program this year was to allow students to expand their knowledge on how different cultures celebrate their holidays and allows us to become a community.

The Academy for Language & Technology offers students courses in Music Technology and Digital Art Editing. Students are able to take courses in Adobe Photoshop, Web Design, Adobe Premier Pro, and Digital Music Design.

q40_r1_c1_4: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
q42_1_rev: At International High School at Prospect Heights, we believe that the arts is a core discipline. Like other disciplines, our arts team uses and refines a list of discipline-based learning outcomes, in addition to schoolwide outcomes for language and collaborative learning. We leverage interdisciplinary curriculum to help students understand the complexity and beauty in their own experiences and the world around them. As a small school, we highly value our arts partnerships. Classroom residencies help bring learning to life, introduce students to career professionals, and diversify the ways in which students can express their ideas. We also rely on arts partnerships to help us connect students to outside programming when their interests exceed our course catalogue.

At P.S./M.S. 42, students that learned remotely began the year receiving music and technology instruction, while students in-person received theater and art 1-2 times a week. In January, remote students began to receive instruction in visual arts and theater once a week. Our school has continued to work with outside organizations like THRIVE and Braata Productions to bring more arts opportunities to the students virtually. The artists at our school (both remote and in-person) have participated in contests and festivals like PS Art, Queens Borough Arts Festival, American Voices, Illustrate Against Hate, and other opportunities set forward by the DOE and community. Next year we will open our Verizon Innovative Learning Schools (VILS) lab, brought to us through a Verizon Grant, and engage students in courses about virtual reality and 3D printing.  The arts are alive and continue to grow at P.S./M.S. 42!

We are committed to high standards in arts education. The arts help children learn creativity, confidence, self-expression, thinking skills, and a joy for learning. We provide arts education by following the NYCDOE Blueprint for the Arts Benchmarks. Due to COVID-19, we were unable to participate in certain activities that we have enjoyed in the past. However, we were about to provide our students, both blended and remote, the following:
CASA: 25 students grades 3-4-5:
Teaching Artists: Queens Performing Arts Center  - The Broadway Experience

CASA - We are excited to offer your child an exciting opportunity to participate in our CASA - After School Broadway Musical Workshop funded by Council Member Karen Koslowitz.  Students took center stage virtually, meeting & working with different Broadway artists. They learned about, and discussed, one of the Broadway musicals that this particular artist had appeared in had the opportunity to learn a musical number from the show. At the conclusion of the program, each student received, via mail, a Broadway workshop t-shirt AND a workshop highlight video.

Students were provided program scheduling in school with the music teacher up to twice a week per class. Students were also provided remote opportunities to engage with teachers for extracurricular arts and STEAM programs. During Remote Learning, our International Festival celebrated the diversity of our school through the performing arts.
Arts instruction at High School for Civil Rights consisted of a visual arts curriculum recommended by New Visions for Public Schools.

During the 2020-2021 school year the arts team at P.S. 24 Andrew Jackson included three full-time visual arts teachers and one full-time music teacher. In addition, our school has a full-time Science, Technology, Engineering and Math (STEM) teacher that incorporates coding and 3D printing. Each arts discipline is aligned with the New York State Standards, as well as the New York City Blueprints for the Arts. The PreK-5 curriculums have a multi-level arts learning experience. Student progress was measured in a variety of ways, including rubrics, checklists, performance assessments, quizzes, portfolios and projects. Monthly newsletters and the Class Dojo app is used to communicate with parents. As the curriculum changed to remote learning, students were also evaluated on video recordings, video reflections and small group virtual conferences. We had a schoolwide virtual Lantern Making Festival for the Lunar New Year where students and their families participated. In June, we had a virtual visual arts show where students and parents participated. The Book of the Month incorporates an art-making component throughout the year. For the Museum of the Month students learn and explore about a new museum virtually. Our dance teacher also has monthly virtual dance parties for students and parents. A few of our classes had a visit from an art educator from the Noguchi Museum who spoke to our students. Our arts team and STEM teacher attend professional development to stay informed and up to date on new offerings in the arts and technology.

TAG Young Scholars School has been devoted to providing well-rounded arts education for its students. All of our students, kindergarten through eighth grade receive consistent, high-quality instruction in music and visual arts. We have a dedicated kindergarten through 4th grade music teacher. In 4th grade, students transition to instrumental music through the recorder. By 5th grade, students choose a band instrument and begin their performance instruction. All kindergarten through 8th grade students perform for their classmates as well as parents during formal concerts multiple times per year. In addition to our music program that takes place during our regular school day, we have an afternoon Latin Jazz Ensemble that rehearses afterschool twice a week. They perform multiple times per year, both in the school and at community events throughout New York City. In addition, our K-4 music teacher also teaches choir to students in grades 6-8.  Our visual arts program is continuing to grow and develop. All of our students, kindergarten through 8th grade, receive visual arts instruction at least one time per week. They work in various mediums. Pieces have been displayed at art shows both in the school and online through Artsonia. Our art teacher also does an "Art Lunch” where students can work on projects during their lunch.

Our program consists of student classes in visual arts, music and dance as electives offered in our building.  These classes include Guitar, Jazz Band, Core Music, Chorus, Art, Studio Art, Painting and Dance.

We offer Basic Studio Arts for the required graduation credits. This class introduces students to a variety of arts mediums and practices to broaden their understanding of the importance of the arts, creativity, and design thinking in the real world. They will make connections between the art that is practiced in class to real world application, worldwide practices, and necessity in culture and society. We also offer an Introduction to Music class. This course allows students to express their creativity through song creation. The students also learn how to play musical instruments.

Public School 347 has been very fortunate to share a dynamic licensed visual arts teacher and a motivated licensed dance teacher with the hign school in our building. Their time is split between the two schools, so we are able to offer dance for half of the year and visual arts for the second half. During a typical school year (and this year was anything but), we would supplement the in-school instruction with visits to the many cultural experiences that NYC offers. Even though this year barred us from venturing out, the teachers have been very proactive in bringing our students to virtual venues to experience art and dance beyond the school walls. By taking advantage of free virtual programs this year, we were able to offer our students  sporadic "field trips" to spark their creative minds. Our arts teachers also took it upon themselves to write a grant that was shared between the high school and our school to purchase additional supplies. Through a grant for English Language Learners and Students with Disabilities in the Arts, Children's Museum of the Arts was able to provide additional art classes for our Pre-K through 8th grade students. Many of our students come from households where the first language is not English. The arts allow all students to express themselves in a langauge that everyone understands.

Our school relies on the talents and interests of our teachers for our arts provisions as well as work with Manhattan School of Music.  This year Manhattan School of Music provided one-on-one vocal coaching for six students and is giving one additional student a free summer class of her choice.  Additionally, we offer art history, music history, and the ever popular crocheting where we mailed home the crochet kits this year.  That is a very popular class even remotely.  We also hosted a string of movies as part of our community building.

Public School 163 has an arts program taught by in-school, full-time dedicated and certified visual arts and music teachers. While this year presented unique situations and uncertainty, our school has been traditionally focused on the arts. For the majority of this year, kindergarten through fifth grade students received instruction twice every three weeks but transitioned to weekly instruction for the last quarter as schools moved toward higher occupancy. Performances by The Voices of 163 usually present three concerts during the year. While this was not possible this year, virtual performances were hosted. Due to the circumstances this year, we were not able to host outside cultural institutions to work with students as usual. Therefore, partnering with organizations such as the Lincoln Center Film Society Kids, the National Dance Institute, and Young Audiences New York was paused. However, Public School 163 worked with non-profit Thrive Collective to carry out a school mural project. Public School 163 also normally hosts the District 3 district-wide art festival every year at the end of May.
New Heights Middle School has a full-time dance teacher and dance studio.  New Heights Middle School incorporates the arts into a comprehensive National Broadway Junior program.

P.S. 191 Mayflower offered virtual assembly programs, virtual arts programs and virtual music assemblies.In all of our arts programs, we wanted the students to learn the value of literary through the arts, oral and cultural traditions, musical and vocal performing, dance, and art appreciation. They learned to express themselves, work together and develop confidence.

Ebbets Field Middle School (EFMS) believes that the arts are a fundamental part of a well-rounded education and are a necessary outlet for students to apply and experiment with concepts from other fields. EFMS views the arts as a place to bring together subject strands from English Language Arts (ELA) to science, and math to engineering. As such, the arts at EFMS are infused throughout content areas, and arts teachers take a multi-disciplinary and project-based approach to instruction. The EFMS Arts Department employs one full-time arts teacher in music.  Numerous opportunities are also provided by engaging cultural partners and teaching artists to supplement and expand upon classroom work, including Ifetayo Cultural Center, HONK NYC, the New York Philharmonic, Carnegie Hall’s Ensemble Connect, Broadway Jr., Brooklyn Music School and BRIC Media Arts. All students from grades 6-8 take music seeing each teacher two times a week. In music, students are exposed to the breadth and diversity of musical genres and instruments around the world. They focus on the cultural context within which musical movements have grown, and they apply this knowledge both to songwriting and on an instrument of their choice by learning the fundamentals of technique, performance, and composition. Students have the opportunity to showcase their work multiple times a year at student award dinners, school assemblies, district events, cultural partner events and our annual Night of the Arts.

Community School 55 has a partnership with Windows Of HipHop. This year we had a music, visual arts, and dance program. We are planning on opening a Windows of HipHop Music studio in 2021. We also have a partnership with Education Through Music and we had a full-time music teacher. Finally, we have partnerships with SCAN Harbor and the Bronx Children's Museum to provide afterschool music options.

Our arts curriculum at I.S. 281 Joseph B. Cavallaro is an integral part of a solid educational foundation that builds upon prior arts knowledge and experience and addresses the needs of all learners. We offer a wide range of experiences in dance,music, media, technology, and visual arts, wherein students develop the physical, aesthetic and critical thinking skills that enable them to see and respond to the world. Students will experience various disciplines to expand their knowledge and skill and help them to make personal connections with our school and the world around them. Technology and visual arts are infused into curriculum studies throughout our school community. Our staff plan units of study that allow students to experience the arts through a variety of media. Ultimately, we seek to nurture an appreciation of the arts within all of our children.

At P.S. 154, we believe that instruction in the arts is essential in providing a well-rounded curriculum for our students. Since children learn in different ways, it is essential to support their learning styles and intelligences using various methods. We have found that the arts can make the difference between a child's success or failure in school. Our goal is to expose our young learners to multiple forms of art so they may experiment and find those that interest them. We continue to expand on these experiences for our young learners and look forward to growing this initiative by partnering with more organizations and providing our students with more enrichment program opportunities.

Even though this year was a challenging one, P.S. 194 has kept the arts alive. Our certified arts teachers and classroom teachers continued to work collaboratively to provide arts instruction to support units of study aligned with the Core Curriculum State Standards, the NYC Blueprints for the Arts and the NYS Learning Standards for the Arts. This year we continued our arts partnerships with Covenant Ballet, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, New York City Center and Midori Foundation.  These workshops reached our in-person and remote students by providing virtual workshops with a teaching artist and recorded performances. This year we received an extension to the English Language Learners/Students with Disabilities and the Arts grant. This grant allowed us to once again have our 4th graders (remote & in-person) participate in an 8 week residency with Covenant Ballet. Many of our grades this year used dance to create video performances that were shared with the school community. Our students have also created many visual arts projects. Two of our students will have work displayed in PS Art and The Brooklyn Borough Arts Festival. Our arts team consists of two certified arts teachers (dance & visual arts). We continue to use our fully renovated dance studio and visual arts rooms for instruction. Our classroom teachers are also continuing our Artist/Composer of the Month program. All of our students, remote and in-person, receive arts instruction and will continue to, as school reopens fully next year. The arts are and will continue to be an integral part of P.S. 194.

We have two major goals in developing the arts at P.S. 173 Fresh Meadows. We plan to continue to train classroom teachers to incorporate more arts learning into the content areas, and we intend to continue to increase students' awareness and appreciation of the arts, parent involvement and outside partnerships in the arts.

At the Manhattan School for Children, we believe that the arts are vital to our children's education and that the exploration of the arts nurtures their creativity, imagination and ability to see other points of view as they make personal connections to the world they live in. To foster this vision, the school community has developed a dynamic and well-organized arts program across arts disciplines that is inclusive of our children's backgrounds and of the world's cultures. We are committed to a vision of the school as a community of learners who are empowered to create their work and share their process. We achieve this vision by the integration of the arts experiences within classroom curriculum and the broad exposure to the arts through our collaborations with neighborhood cultural institutions. With the need for virtual education, K-8th grade students studying at home, we're working to maximize online instruction, use of videos and collaborative presentations virtually. We believe that art, culture and creativity will continue to be at the forefront at our school.

Essex Street Academy offers three electives for students in the arts: visual arts, theater and music. In the visual arts program, students use a variety of media and learn art history through the study of contemporary and classical artists. Students create a series of works that reflects growth and mastery of technique. In our theater program, students learn memorization skills, performance tactics and perform major scenes from a variety of theatrical genres. Our music program is a performance-based curriculum that focuses on building foundational skills and nurturing a lifelong relationship to music. The students learn and practice vocal and beat making skills and participate in talent shows and an end of year art expo.  All three electives are offered to students in all four grades and end in a performance based assessment task.

P.S. 217 Colonel David Marcus School's goal is to provide all students with sequential instruction in the arts so they meet benchmarks in the NYC Blueprints for the Arts.  Students experienced instruction in visual arts, music, and theater from our certified arts teachers and additional instruction in visual art, theater and dance through arts organization residencies. Students K-5 also experienced additional instruction in the arts through our afterschool club program which offered instruction in theater, music and dance.

I.S. 61 Leonardo Da Vinci has offered a complete performing and visual arts program, which includes theater, music (band and strings), visual arts, media arts, and dance for the past ten years. Our students participated in virtuallly in visual arts, dance, film, music, and theater classes. They were engaged as our teachers worked hard to move their arts classrooms into the virtual world. As a school community we worked diligently to keep the arts alive for our students.  Teachers were teaching afterschool to keep our students motivated and engaged in the arts.

During this challenging year, P.S. 179 Kensington has continued to provide arts programming for students, including visual arts instruction, along with virtual and in-person art programs through NIA Community Service Network and 21st Century Grant.   Our school looks forward to school year 2021-2022, as we resume full arts programming.

We have a dual licensed English Language Arts/Theater Arts teacher that teaches two sections of Arts/Theater per trimester. The teacher also partnered with the Stellar Acting Theater which provided both school residencies and multiple off-site opportunities for our students.

The Gordon Parks School for Inquisitive Minds Arts Program continues to inspire and encourage excellence. Students in all grades have the opportunity to participate in a wide variety of artistic endeavors. Extra-curricular programs are available before, during, and after school in Dance, Chorus, Recorder, Violin, Ukulele, Modern Band, Drumline, Visual Arts, and Theater.

At the Fresh Creek School we believe in educating the whole child. At the heart of this philosophy is a commitment to providing all of our students with opportunities to develop their many intelligences. To that end, we provided instruction in music and visual arts to every child. This year, using the Orf Method, we focused on developing a percussion and winds program, including training in the use of the recorder, African drums, and xylophone. Students also engaged in vocal training and choral singing. Our students received instruction in digital art making, video production, and digital music production. For our early childhood learners, we offered puppetry to develop their theater and music skills.

Virtual general music instruction was made available to PK-5th grade students in hybrid groups from September 2020 to December 2021. During the school year, hybrid students in grades K, 2nd, and 4th grade had in-person music instruction during the instructional lunch periods: two or three times a week. The 4th and 5th-grade students had a chance to participate in the PS 68X Chorus/Orff Ensemble.  The rehearsals were once-a-week,60 minutes via Zoom, the students learned to sing and play the soprano and alto recorder.  The Music/Recorder club was made available to all 4th and 5th-grade students once a week for 60 minutes as well.
