Since 1997, Education Through Music, Inc. has partnered with PS 68X. Regrettably, because of in-person learning restrictions, we could not have a string orchestra.  However, ETM provided support and professional development opportunities for the DOE-employed general music teacher at PS 68X, Ms. Tanisha D. Campbell. Hopefully, the string orchestra program will resume in the fall.
PS 68X has worked with the Inside Broadway/CASA program for several years as well. The program was run virtually this year; it ends in virtual performance.
In addition, afterschool services in the creative arts are provided by the Phipps Community Development Corporation, which provides instruction to our in-person students. 
Unfortunately, we were not able to continue the visual arts instruction.  We look forward to visual arts instruction resuming in the near future.

Our current arts program at Riverdale Avenue Community School consists of full-time programs in music, visual arts, and multi media. All units are aligned with the NYC Blueprints for the Arts and NYS Learning Standards for the Arts. Teachers collaborated on a virtual performance this year. Partnerships with the Jazz at Lincoln Center group was a great virtual experience for the students this year.

Through immersion and collaborations with various cultural programs, our students develop talent and skills in different areas of the arts. The arts are integrated into our interdisciplinary curriculum with a focus on the development of literacy, cultural appreciation, and integration of the curriculum. The programs of study actively engage children in experiencing the arts and communicating through them. We have collaborations with Chen Dance Center, The Drawing Center, Dancing Classrooms, Audubon Society, Center for Architecture, Midori & Friends, Faces of Wonder, New Victory Theater, YMCA, and Third Street Music School Settlement. The residencies are aligned with the core curriculum to support classroom instruction and provide professional development for participating staff including parental participation. We have two highly qualified arts teachers providing in-house music and visual arts instruction and experiences to the students. Gallery walks, art exhibits, celebrations, and concerts are held throughout the school year. An invitation to all these events is extended to all members of the Public School 42 community.

Here at P.S. 340 we value and support a well-rounded arts eduction that is interdisciplinary with a range of subjects. In particular, the arts curriculum has direct alignment throughout the year with Passport to Social Studies and Civics For All correlating art projects with a range of social studies and civics units. Students exercise both their oral and written language abilities through goal setting, critiques, artist statements and reflective writing pieces. A large push this year in the arts programing was aligning identity work done in the classroom with identity based art projects in the art classroom. In addition, students studied a range of historical and contemporary artists from different countries and cultures. Next year P.S.340 has the intention of adding a music teacher to the school base staff with the purchasing of instruments to expand arts exposure for our students.
At World Academy for Total Community Health High School, students studied music virtually.

P.S. 16 The Nancy DeBenedittis School strives to align its curriculum with the NYC Blueprints for the Arts, implement school-wide enrichment and accelerate learning for each student in music, visual arts, dance and theater. Our school strives to enrich the curriculum through morning arts programs, daily school arts programming, monthly field trips, residencies and implementation of enrichment clusters in the arts during the day and in an after school rotating program. Our school hopes to sustain partnerships with cultural organizations in the arts including the Dancing Classrooms, and Dance Wave. Our school will continue to seek and forge new alliances to further enhance arts programming.

P.S. 212 Lady Deborah Moody places a very high priority on the quality of the arts imparted to our children. The administration supports every effort to create and maintain an environment that embraces the arts and reflects the cultural diversity of the students that attend our school. Through our dance and visual arts programs, students study cultures, history, and modern art forms that depict social issues in our world. We celebrate the arts through exhibits, performances, and culminating events for art residencies. This year, the arts have taken on a role virtually that has helped us connect both in- person and remotely. Workshops were offered virtually to all students and provided an opportunity for all students in our community to work together to learn and engage in the arts
We continue to offer drama classes and play writing opportunities as well as music history and visual arts classes and dance as a club.

P.S. 203 Floyd Bennett School’s engaging arts education program continues to grow and thrive. We understand the need for high quality arts for all students and the importance of early immersion in the arts, especially after a year where most of our students learned remotely and had little to no direct access to the arts.  Our school plans to offer a balanced arts program - visual arts, music, band, and dance, whether led by a certified arts teacher or classroom teacher. We are continuously making strides to exceed the expectations as set forth in the Blueprints for the Arts and through the integration of the NYS Common Core Art Standards. Our seasonal performances, school-based and cultural organization-based assemblies, annual theater production, music and visual arts residencies, chorus, band, and annual art festival continue to develop and showcase the talent of our students and staff. Student performances and presentations are among the highlights of the school year and support with parent/guardian presence.  It is with great excitement that we have begun to utilize the City Council $250,000 grant to update our auditorium with theater lighting and sound and a fully stocked control booth.

Students were provided arts instruction in is visual arts and theater by certified on-site teachers.  A partnership developed with a community-based organization to provide dance instruction for middle school students.

At Francis Lewis High School, our current arts program consists of dance, theater, visual arts, graphic arts, and vocal and orchestral/band performances. Our goals are to sustain a diverse and challenging sequence of courses which will culminate with various performances in and out of school. Our Celebration of the Arts will showcase art (literature, performance, visual ) by our students and staff in hopes of promoting cultural and the social-emotional development of our school community. Our students are exposed to authentic arts experiences outside of the classroom, including performances, trips, and presentations by guest speakers, organizations, and post-secondary institutions. Many of our students get accepted and earn scholarships to colleges and universities specifically for the arts.

There are two Career and Technical Education (CTE ) arts programs housed at Bayside High School: The Digital Art & Design Program and The Music & Audio Production Program. Students in both tracks receive core CTE courses blended with traditional arts instruction. Both programs award students with up to nine college credits in their respective arts concentrations. Each track culminates in a capstone project and professional certification exam. Our goal is that students graduate college and career ready.

There are several goals that are incorporated into the arts program at PS 47: Goal 1- to provide a variety of art disciplines and create a continuum from k to 5 that will allow children to explore and discover their talents; Goal 2- to develop a lifelong love and appreciation for the arts; Goal 3- to infuse the arts into all content areas, allowing teachers to provide differentiation based on individual student modalities and talents. PS 47 has adopted the Reggio Emelia philosophy which originated in Southern Italy. This philosophy is basically a ""projects approach"" to literacy and content area studies. Through the Reggio Emelia philosophy, children work cooperatively to develop art projects and culminating activities that include researching, writing, and oral presentations; Goal 4- to align the arts with the New York State Standards for the Arts; creating and performing in the arts; knowing and using arts materials and resources; responding to and analyzing works of art.

The Corona Arts and Sciences Academy continues to provide high quality, in depth arts education that is rich in content, practice and accessibility to all students. We continue to add new arts teachers and programs. This year, even in the midst of a global pandemic, we were not only able to keep our programs intact, but added media arts to the pantheon of programs that we offer at our school. Live and blended students received arts instruction and participated in virtual performances and exhibitions throughout the school year. As a result, we are well positioned for a full recovery of our arts programs next year. We look forward to a bright and vibrant arts filled 2021-22 school year.

Visual arts students are introduced to a variety of art materials and techniques with a focus on creating, observing, speaking about and writing about art. Students become familiar with various artists and art movements from around the world and throughout history and work independently and in groups to create art projects that incorporate a wide array of artistic concepts and materials. Students work on projects that deepen their knowledge of the Elements of Art as they develop their own artistic style and voice. Projects are often connected to the social studies curricula. In dance, students are introduced to a variety of dance styles and techniques with highly trained professional dancers through a series of residencies. Students work in groups to create dance routines. Dance techniques are taught across the grades and are age and developmentally appropriate. Starting in second grade, students perform choreographed dances at the culmination of their residencies. Theater is provided with classroom teachers to support social studies instruction through drama. Our music program introduces a variety of music making activities, including vocal, instrumental, and percussive. Students become familiar with various artists, styles, and genres from around the world and various time periods. Students work together and alone to create new pieces of music as well as to perform vocal and instrumental music in a variety of genres.

At I. S. 381, all students sixth through eighth grade have been given the opportunity to take visual arts, dance and or music during the 2020-2021 academic year,in person as well as virtual. Students receive one to two periods per week of one or more art disciplines, plus extra visual arts instruction during an enrichment program. Students interested in visual arts portfolios for visual arts high schools are given the opportunity to continue their visual arts process through visual arts clubs given each day during their lunch time, as well as an afternoon enrichment program offered in the spring. As we move forward to the 2021-2022 school year, we are committed to engaging all students in the arts through in-person instruction.

PS/IS 208 has been partnering with Arts Connection for the past ten years. This year Arts Connection faciltated a virtual film residency during after school hours. We believe that the arts are an essential part of middle school education and have set aside time during after school hours to make this happen. In the past, our elective classes included Dance, Music, Art, and Film. We used the funding from an ELL/SWD (English Language Learners/Students With Disabilities) grant to broaden student choice during our electives and included Film, which taught our students how to create stop motion credit sequences and "love poem" animations. In the past few years, we've created a Musical Theater Program with the help of MTI (Music Theater International/Shubert Broadway Jr) Grant. This two-year program is designed to assist PS/IS 208 in developing a sustainable, quality theater program which engages our students in the joyful process of creating musical theater. It helps foster a strong educational community as students, staff, and families all "play a role" in the process and can also encourage the connection of arts programming to curriculum study in all content areas. Our students performed Fame Jr., Willy Wonka Kids, Shrek Jr., Hairspray Jr., and The Wiz. These performances allowed our students to tap into their creative side and express themselves in multiple ways. In addition to acting, singing and dancing, the students created the set design and were in charge of cueing the music for the performances. Arts in schools helps shape lives!

The performing arts department at The High School for Enterprise, Business and Technology (EBT) is one of the biggest and best in NYC. We have four full concert bands, two jazz bands, music theater, and numerous chamber groups such as guitar ensemble and Latin jazz band. Students have the option of majoring in music. Over 600 students receive music instruction each day. The instrumental, theater, and general music programs draw from all three schools in the campus and allow students to perform at their ability level regardless of age or experience. All musical ensembles compete annually at the NYSSMA festival where they have received Gold and Gold with Distinction awards. In addition to our performing groups, students may take classes in technical theater which prepares students for jobs in the entertainment industry focusing on stage direction, lighting and sound. Our visual arts department offers students instruction in the foundations of drawing and painting. Advanced students may move on to studio art classes and Advanced Placement Art History. Students are given the opportunity to participate in the All City High School Concert Band and Marching Band both of which are hosted at the Grand Street Campus.

Public School 64, Home of Music and Art for Young Minds, has continued to blossom over the past several years. Equity remains a top priority, and as such, every student in Pre-Kindergarten through fifth grade receives comprehensive and sequential instruction in visual arts, music and dance. Students’ work is showcased and celebrated throughout the year in hallway displays, art shows, mini performances, schoolwide concerts, and student assemblies. The music, dance, and visual arts rooms are outfitted with all necessary materials and equipment to fully engage our students in a rich curriculum as outlined by the NYCDOE Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. Our seasoned arts teachers guide students in making meaningful connections between the arts and the world around them. Additional dance, theater and visual arts instruction is supported by classroom teachers and several community based organizations, including New York City Ballet, Dancing Classrooms, and Rosie’s Theater Kids. Our students participate in many field trips to museums, cultural institutions, concert halls, and Broadway theaters. We have a full-time certified dance, music, and visual arts teacher on our staff providing every student a foundation of technical skills while developing their artistry. P.S. 64 is proud of its dedication to the arts and will continue to provide high quality arts education to the community we serve.

At the Global Learning Collaborative, all ninth grade students are in enrolled in dance. Students have the opportunity to continue to take dance courses as electives. Our school also offers advanced dance classes. Our dance course is aligned with our school's mission and commitment to global learning. Arts teachers actively participate in team meetings with teachers of other disciplines to ensure a well- rounded program. This creates a unified curriculum committed to the support of the arts from a global perspective. All tenth graders are enrolled in ceramics which has a strong basis in science education, global perspectives as well as connection to math in the arts. Students in grades eleven and twelve may take ceramics level II. We also offer two Advanced Placement (AP) art and design classes which is connected to AP for All program. Students who would like to take the AP art courses are allowed two years to develop portfolios. Students can begin to take AP art and design their junior year. During their senior year, the AP art course is dedicated to final development of strong portfolio submissions. Field trip experiences to museums and dance performances are embedded in our dance and ceramics programs. Students are also afforded opportunities to attend art workshops at the Metropolitan Museum of Art and Musem of Arts and Design. Other dance opportunities are abundant thanks to partnerships with National Dance Education Organization and New York State Dance Education Association.

Aligned with the NYS Standards and the NYC Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts, 7th grade students were provided with music instruction, and 8th grade students were provided with visual arts instruction. In music, students learn about key moments in music history and a basic knowledge of music theory and notation.  They have opportunities to compose music using technology, including the digital music programs Soundtrap and Chrome Music Lab Song Maker. Due to health regulations, students were unable to utilize the guitar lab this year. In visual arts, students learn to use a variety of art media and techniques, including digital media, along with studying many artists and their work. Students learn to critique their own work and the work of other students. We collaborate with our school-based organization, Learning through an Expanded Arts Program (LeAp), for several afterschool arts programs. Our music teacher maintains the MS 129 Guitar Ensemble by holding virtual band class after school. They will be again performing in the Bronx Borough Arts Festival. This year we were one of the middle schools selected for the Shubert Foundation/MTI Broadway Junior program. Students participated in weekly rehearsals and performed the first-ever virtual production of Shrek, Jr. at MS 129. For the 2021-2022 school year, we plan to launch a Graphic Design studio class, where students will receive technology through arts instruction and experience the use of our new 3D printer lab.

q40_r1_c1_4: Learning Through an Expanded Arts Program (LEAP)
q40_r1_c1_3: Learning Through an Expanded Arts Program (LEAP)
q42_1_rev:
Jonas Bronck Academy looks to integrate the arts into our middle school curriculum. Over the course of 3 years, students will receive one full year of visual Art as well as a full year of dance.
The school also looks to supplement our school day programs with outside opportunities provided by our partner CBO (Learning through an Expanded Arts Program -LEAP) and other cultural institutions when available. After school opportunities include, dance, art, photography, film, film studies, fashion, publishing, theater and musical productions, as well as band and chorus.

Our school currently has one certified visual arts teacher that is teaching visual arts to 6, 7 and 8 grade  students in our school. Each class has visual arts at least 2 - 3 times per week. Community based organizations, Counseling in Schools and New York Edge, provide finger painting.

The Cultural Academy for the Arts and Sciences (CAAS) offers students a visual arts program that has an art historical component alongside hands-on exposure to a wide range of media, including drawing, painting and sculpture. Our students also explore theater, the spoken word, music, and culinary arts. The culinary program is in its fifth year, and provides students with experiences anchored in the restaurant industry. Culinary students hone their skills through internships, catering a variety of school events, as well as running a lunch cafe. The recipient of a 21st Century Grant, CAAS has a full-service after school program, which is run by the Leadership Program, featuring music production, mural painting, karate, culinary arts, and theater arts. In addition to project-based learning in visual arts, cultural literacy is built into the school day. Students are exposed to theater and film production and participate in talent shows at least once a year. Students attend gallery exhibits and enter visual arts competitions, including the Scholastic Art Awards and PS Art. Many of our students' work have been exhibited at the Brooklyn Borough Hall, Tweed Court House, Brooklyn Children's Museum, and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. CAAS is a steadfast supporter of its in-service learning through our many partnerships. Our students participate in a host of residencies and performances at the Brooklyn Academy of Music involving Shakespeare, the spoken word, as well as storytelling.

At P.S. 281, our goal is to ensure that students receive a well-rounded education where the arts balance the academics. We strive to provide students with a varied arts curriculum through school-based arts teachers and outside organizations. As we continue to grow and receive grant funding, we hope to cultivate partnerships with cultural institutions in New York City so our students can reap the benefits of learning in a cultural hub of the world. Ultimately, our goal is for the arts to become integrated with classroom curriculum and to bring the academic content to life. All students at P.S. 281 receive instruction in visual arts and music by full-time arts teachers. The music program is centered around core musical skills and developing a life long appreciation and understanding of music. Students sing a variety of repertoire and learn to play percussion instruments, Orff instruments, piano, recorder, ukulele, and guitar. They develop skills to move expressively, improvise, compose, and read and write music. The visual arts program, started in the fall of 2019, is geared toward teaching for artistic behavior. Students develop studio habits of mind, including experimenting with art materials, practicing techniques, visualizing their ideas, honing their observation skills, reflecting on their practice, and contextualizing their work within the global artistic community. Students develop skills in drawing, painting, collage, sculpture, ceramics, and printmaking.

Brooklyn Environmental Exploration School (BEES) is a small middle school. As such, we use a variety of means to incorporate the arts into our programming. We have a visual arts teacher and all students take a visual arts classes two periods per week. This year we partnered with The Town Hall Foundation for three separate in-school artist residencies. We hosted The Town Hall teaching artists in dance, theater and creative writing; all students participated in the residencies. Additionally, we are a New Victory theater education partner school. This means BEES students attend virtual performances often at New Victory on 42nd Street.

Currently, we have a certified visual arts teacher who services the students in our school. The visual arts teacher  helps the teachers connect visual arts to all of the content areas and assists the students with projects. In addition, the visual arts teacher facilitates parent workshops twice a month showing them how visual arts connects to what their children are learning in school. This is our sixth year having schoolwide enrichment clubs once a week. Every Tuesday students participate in clubs that are arts based. We have a partnership with the New York City Ballet which services our third and fourth graders.

Students explore a wide range of media and complete individual and collaborative projects. Painting, drawing, printmaking, and sculpture are all part of the curriculum. Students are encouraged to be inventive and original. The curriculum is designed to build on art skills and experiences as students advance through the grades.  
Music instruction sequential and comprehensive for all students in the school. Students learn about proper singing techniques in a choir to become musically literate. Students also learn to play musical instruments in an ensemble.
Due to the pandemic we did not have any performances this year. Our former art teacher retired and we are actively looking for a new art teacher.

Our arts program is an integral part of our students’ academic program. During the school day, all students enroll in arts-based electives, including Instrumental Music, Visual Arts, Dance, Performing Arts, Computer Design, Crafts, and Woodworking. All of our freshmen take a Fundamentals of Art course and attend two art-based field trips in their first year of high school. Three fourths of our sophomores take a Beginner's Photography class while a quarter of the cohort moved on to an Advanced Photography course. Upperclassmen have access to more advanced courses like Pottery and Advanced Painting. After school, there are a series of arts-based programs open to all students, including dance, visual arts, 3D printing, and music. During the summer, we run "Camp AMS," an all-day program combining academics and arts. This camp is open to all middle school students, including those mandated for summer school. Throughout the year, all of our arts programs include performances and displays. Students invite the community to share and celebrate their acquired artistic skills.

Union Square Academy for Health Sciences (U.S.A.) continues to be committed to providing a rich arts experience for all students. With a full-time music teacher and the investment of an electric piano keyboard lab, students in grades 9-12 are immersed in a comprehensive arts curriculum based on units and lessons designed around the New York State Learning Standards for the Arts and NYCDOE Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts and the Common Core Standards. Music Making, Music Literacy, Music History, Cultural Connections and Life-Long Careers in the Arts were the major themes of study this year. In addition to the NYS Standards for Learning in the Arts based curriculum, a special focus was placed on social-emotional learning this year. Students had the opportunity and responsibility to become educated readers, writers, performers and appropriate audience members and to give and receive constructive feedback to each other. The majority of U.S.A. students were opted for remote-instruction due to the global pandemic, but that did not stop our students from continuing to "create, present, produce and respond" in music class. We expanded our use of technology this year, and we look very much forward to coming back together in person stronger than ever for the 2021-2022 school year at Union Square Academy For Health Sciences. We are planning our events and musical performances.

J.H.S. 259 William Mckinley takes pride in providing its students with a varied choice of arts disciplines during the day in order to explore and expand their creative needs and inspire lifelong arts learners. Students also have the opportunity to pursue a new arts skill during afterschool programs. Afterschool programs include: drama club, dance, keyboard, marching band, concert band, scenic design, and fashion club. One of our most exceptional features is a 400 foot mural on our third floor which has been featured on CBS, ABC, and Fox television. This remarkable piece showcases the talents of our students interweaving history, poetry, and literature of various periods in collaboration with the 9/11 Tribute Center. Additionally, we have an installation that meshes the arts and science in a salute to the Renaissance. This school year we were able to incorporate a mural on the first floor, which encompasses and celebrates all the diversity that can be seen at McKinley.  Our goal for the 2021-2022 school year is to allow more opportunities for students to engage in the arts. After a remote learning year, it is time for us to bring the arts back into our building.

P.S. 748 Brooklyn School for Global Scholars continues to use an interdisciplinary approach to integrate visual and performing arts into the curriculum. This year, due to the pandemic, instruction in the arts has been provided by classroom teachers. As the Arts remain a priority, we have committed to partnerships with the Midori Foundation and Marquis Studios to support our students in all grades, as well as our teachers in Arts Education. We hosted a virtual dance festival to adhere to social distancing guidelines and in an effort to maintain the health and safety of our school community. We have supplemented our curriculum with virtual field trips, but we look forward to September when we return to in-person instruction and work towards strengthening our arts curriculum experiences for our students.

Seth Low I.S. 96 is proud to offer a variety of performing and visual arts to cultivate the talent of our students. All students receive general instruction in both visual arts and music in 6th through 8th grades. In addition, students can choose to take part in the following specialties: visual arts (including drawing and painting), theater, vocal, orchestra, band or drum corps. In addition, we are a Broadway Junior School, and our students perform for various audiences, including peers, parents, and the community.

This year Arts was limited due to the pandemic.  Our hope and our plans are to once again infuse our school with various opportunities in the arts in order to expose and develop well rounded students. 
We look forward to continuing our relationship with DreamYard and to offer our students a variety of activities in dance, music, theatre, photography as well as incorporate more digital platforms to showcase students' work in addition to the art exhibit displays we showcase in school.

Arts has always played a significant role in the life of our school. We have an extensive Advanced Placement 2D Arts program that offers students of all languages a chance to express themselves and earn college credit. In addition to introductory to art courses and Edgenuity courses, art is integrated into the general classes. Lincoln Center Theater has been a valuable partner in offering in-house theater residencies to our English Languages Learners providing them the opportunity to find their voice, learn English and gain confidence through theater activities. Normally we have the opportunity to provide for students to view Broadway shows, Ballet Hispanico and visit museums throughout New York City. Due to COVID, these events were placed on hold, but we plan to engage in these activities next school year. We continue our photography programs with Magic Box Productions, Inc. Students are able to produce talent shows, cultural celebrations, art and photography exhibitions. As always, our goal is to expose our students to culture through the arts and provide them opportunities to which they might not normally have access.

q40_r1_c1_3: Office of Arts and Special Projects
q42_1_rev:
Pathways College Preparatory School is a 6-12 school that offers students in every grade a choice between dance and music arts' electives. Middle school classes meet four times a week. High school classes are mixed grade level and meet anywhere from two to five times a week. The arts program is performance-based, with two large concert venues each year. About five to six other, smaller performances also happen every year. The support for the arts program is very strong within the student body and community. Dance instruction focuses on building technique and student-written choreography. Music instruction varies by grade: 6th and 7th graders form the middle school choir; 8th grade is a percussion ensemble; 9-12th grades are different conglomerations of Modern Band; there is also a select band for advanced high school students.

This year, all classes were virtual, and we had a giant school performance encompassing all arts students that was streamed on YouTube Premiere.

P.S. 327 Dr. Rose B. English is a community school. Our arts programs are provided by The Leadership Program for all enrolled students throughout the school day and the 21st Century Community Learning Center. In addition, our students receive martial arts/capoeira instruction through CARE. Music, theater and dance is provided by OPUS Dance Group throughout the school year by The Leadership Program.

During 2020-21, at P.S. 56 Harry Eichler, we were fortunate to have a full-time music teacher who provided music instruction to all of our students in grades 2-5. Students received music instruction two to three days per week. Our curriculum centers around fulfilling the NYS Core Music Standards. Students play classroom instruments, move and sing to grow as musicians. Students are assessed through participation in arts performance assessments, culminating projects, teacher observation and feedback and written assessments. The goal of the music program is teaching students how to approach complex problems with creativity and innovation, encourage them to develop confidence and emotional maturity, and provide students with an essential form of expression. Our vision is to nurture the development of cognitive, social, and interpersonal competencies.

P.S./I.S. 119 The Glendale offers a variety of performing arts to our students. We presently have a number of orchestras, bands, chorus, chamber winds, Music and the Brain keyboard (for our elementary students), and visual arts. The arts program is designed to connect with the other content areas and to meet National Standards for the Arts and implement the NYC Blueprints for the Arts. Students who audition for high schools in the arts receive individualized instruction to build their portfolios and prepare audition pieces. Parents and the community enjoy our shows and performances throughout the year.

Our goal is to foster an environment where artistic creativity is nurtured and developed. We strive for students to recognize the cultural and societal significance of the arts, thus becoming lifelong advocates. Through our arts program, students are allowed to see themselves as true artists and performers. We believe our arts program helps students to develop critical thinking skills enabling them to view the world through multiple lenses. In this current era of remote learning, our goals have not changed. We continue to support our students with quality arts education. Our arts program is aligned with NYS Arts Standards and NYCDOE Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts.

Shuang Wen School has always prided itself on their academics -- mathematics, literacy, science, AND THE ARTS. We provide music and visual arts instruction for all elementary and middle school students along with some classes of music and art theory. In addition to classroom instruction, students virtually visited a wide range of cultural and community organizations throughout the year. Within the school year, every elementary and middle school student performs and exhibits their work within their classes and for their parents, teachers and the neighborhood community. For the upcoming 2021-2022 school year, Shuang Wen School plans to incorporate additional use of technology and digital design within the arts with a photography program and modern band along with various cultural events for the community within the arts curriculum.

q40_r1_c1_4: Office of Arts and Special Projects
q40_r1_c1_3: Office of Arts and Special Projects
q42_1_rev: Our school enjoys an international reputation as the first and foremost high school dedicated to nurturing students in the arts. Part of our mission is to provide an opportunity for students to pursue conservatory style training. Our state-of-the-art building across from Lincoln Center was designed especially for the arts and features world-class facilities including a 1,150-seat concert hall, visual arts, dance, music, recording and theater studios, and an art gallery.

P.S. 116 Manhattan has a longstanding commitment to aesthetic arts education where students learn by focusing on an artist's works of art, including dance, music, theater, and visual arts. We concentrate on students' perceptions of a particular work guided by a line of inquiry to explore the artistic and aesthetic process of featured artists. In order to provide each child a comprehensive experience with the arts, we are proud partners with 92nd Street Y, American Classical Orchestra, Dancing Classrooms, Jazz at Lincoln Center, and National Dance Institute. During this unprecendented school year, we are grateful that some of our valued partners were able to offer virtual afterschool programming to keep the arts alive at 116!

For the current school year, we have a licensed visual arts teacher servicing students in various classes in grades six through eight, including our English as a New Language (ENL) and Students with Disabilities (SWD) populations. We received a CASA grant again this year and worked with Creative Art Works. Due to Covid-19, we were unable to hold the Creative Art Works classes in-person, but they were able to have virtual workshops for the students. Also, teaching artists from Lincoln Center worked with two of our eighth grade classes virtually which culminated in a performance of a Shakespeare play.

At PS 354 we aim to leverage arts integration through STEM activities. Students are given opportunities to think creatively and explore digital and traditional arts as a method of communication and expression. Through the collaborative use of teaching artists and partnership of our after-school program, students have meaningful opportunities to explore their identity and the world around them through integrated arts opportunities.

P.S. 21 Edward Hart provides a well-rounded arts program for all students. Our third grade students participate in a comprehensive recorder program where they learn to read music as well as play the instrument. This program gives the students a basic music background before they choose an instrument for our fourth/fifth grade band program. Our arts department has collaborated to produce a virtual showcase through our school's multicultural night. Visual Arts exhibits are on display throughout the school building. Each year our dedication to the arts is further developed through a variety of cultural affiliations. This year we are proud of our virtual partnership with Carnegie Hall. All of our grade-wide or school-wide arts events are showcased in order to give our families the opportunity to celebrate their children's accomplishments. We have also continued our arts learning remotely and in-person during this academic school year using a variety of virtual platforms to enhance and implement instruction.

At The Longwood Academy of Discovery, our arts programming reaches all Pre-Kindergarten to Fifth Grade students through classes in visual arts and music, and supplementary services provided through cultural arts organizations.  

Through the arts, we create opportunities for students to build cultural competence (knowledge of their own cultures and the cultures of others); develop skills to become lifelong artistic learners; show pathways to professions in the arts; and provide space for students to expand their learning by engaging in the creative process.

Our students have access to a full visual arts studio, a technology classroom, and a renovated auditorium space that will be upgraded soon.

For the 2020-21 school year, the St. Clair McKelway School continued with an arts program during the school day. Also, a portion of our middle school population was exposed to the arts during our NY Edge SONYC afterschool program which runs each day from 2:30- 4:45. SONYC allows our students to participate in visual arts as well as step/dance classes. The students in SONYC have participated in an visual arts gallery and showcases where their work is displayed, and they engage in musical performances. Classroom teachers have also engaged students in performances, visual arts, and creative writing. The school community loves and values the arts, and we will continue to program our students with arts classes in the 2021-22 school year including either a dance or theater class. We will also apply for grants that will allow us to provide our students with a resident artist during the school day and/or after school.

Our goal for the visual arts program is to provide a four-year arc of meaning-making through a variety of media. Each year students will engage in art making through the lenses of a studio based approach with a focus on the creative process. We will also seek to  explore the theme of identity and our place in our world, both historically and in the present. In addition, real world opportunities and projects will be the foundation of the curriculum. Students will be introduced to maintaining a sketchbook for the collection of ideas, lean heavily into the design process, analyze and interpret a wide range of perspectives represented by multi-ethnic artists, and utilize the vast opportunities to seeing art in person through visiting museums and gallery spaces. With regards to music, the curriculum is designed so that students can derive a meaningful learning experience regardless of prior knowledge and experience in music.

Public School 146Q is proud to offer theater and visual arts classes to all of our students. All students are exposed to music and dance in their regular classroom programs. We have student artwork on display throughout the school year. We schedule virtual and live student trips to for them to be able to experience art forms in music, drama, and dance. We participate in citywide art contests offered by the Office of Health and Wellness, NYC Sustainability Council (Energy Saving), and local politician's Earth Day celebrations. Under the guidance of our theater teacher, multi-grade students put on yearly musicals and/or performances. We believe the arts is an integral piece in the mosaic of each students' well-rounded education. The overall goal of our arts program is to have students in grades Pre-k 3 through grade 8th experience the arts. Additionally, we have observed the arts and the positive impact it has on students with various learning styles and student social and emotional growth. The arts program grows with the child to provide unique opportunities for development, confidence and independence.

Students at Public School 452 study, explore and create in visual arts, architecture, vocal and instrumental music, dance, theatre and media arts/moving image. Cross-curricular units include opportunities both within the classroom and in the multitude of NYC’s artistic spaces, including museums, performance venues, parks, landmarks, studios and cultural institutions. We utilize group projects that require the children to plan, research, organize and share. Our goal-oriented units use technology, visual arts, drama and movement to express ideas. Currently, we engage our primary grade students in the exploration of the foundations of music and begin to foster their visual artist-self through a variety of media. Upper grade students begin to diversify their learning through choral work, differentiated instrumentation, art history, art making, art critique, and advanced visual artistic creation. We believe the arts to be an inclusive and engaging experience for all students, instilling an appreciation for all art forms while fostering their journey to become lifelong fine arts appreciators. During the 2019-2020 school year, we engaged in residency programs with National Dance Institute, the Salvadori Center, New York Historical Society, and Lincoln Center Film Society Kids. We work in collaboration with cultural institutions such as The American Museum of Natural History, Carnegie Hall, and various other museums and artistic institutions throughout New York City.

Middle School 210Q's primary goal is to perform at a level which will include our school in conversations that were once exclusive to arts high schools. The Arts Department has grown exponentially through the guidance of our teachers and cultural partnerships. Our teachers and guest artists have taught our students strategies in public speaking, collaboration, and risk-taking. These efforts have resulted in a noticeable improvement in pride, confidence, community building, and academic performance. This year, we were able to bring arts into our classrooms both in-person and remotely. Students from all grade levels within our building were able to jump into our arts programs, performing, creating and experiencing all of the magic the arts offer our community each year. Our Art Spaces were also recently updated due to the ArtSpace grant. This opportunity has allowed our programs and students to continue to grow and thrive with updated spaces, technology and opportunities. With COVID-19 on the forefront, the arts are an important tool in helping students cope and reflect on these difficult times. The arts will provide students with skills to improve and focus on their social/emotional learning. Creativity is born when challenges are presented. The arts will be there to provide students with a strong community, hope, and a brave place to explore and create.

Our classroom teachers incorporate the arts into their curriculum-Our 4th grade teachers worked with visual arts through our district wide grant with the Guggenheim Museum.  Our goal is to expand our arts program to include dance, theater, and photography.

The High School of Art and Design has been a commercial art high school since 1936. All curricula are developed with our industry partners and post-secondary educational partners. We prepare students for college and careers in the arts. Our students receive two periods of art instruction daily for all four years that they attend our school. Our programs are all NYS approved Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs:  architectural design, cartooning, animation, graphic design, illustration, digital photography, film and video, and fashion design. Students learn the Adobe suite and AutoCAD software programs and become certified in both programs. Our facilities mirror the state-of-the-art equipment used in the industry and students participate in internships available through industry partners and various arts organizations. They compete in art competitions and display their artwork in school and outside venues. Graduating students are accepted into major colleges and universities throughout the country. All our majors have their own gallery shows in the Kenny Gallery throughout the year. We also invite alumni and industry professionals to share their expertise with our students during Career Day. Our culminating Spring Arts Festival thoroughly highlights student achievement in the arts. This year due to Covid-19 we launched a Virtual Arts Festival. In addition, our fashion students presented their fashion show virtually and the film students showcased their films in their virtual online film festival.

We have a Career and Technical Education (CTE) Graphic Design Program which is a seven course sequence of courses leading to a certification in Adobe Illustrator.  Scholars also have an opportunity to work with Lehman College Art Gallery in 9th grade and with CUNY Creative Arts Program in the 10th and 11th grade.  Scholars also have access to internships in their industry through our work-based learning program.

This year in visual arts students are continuing to explore a variety of materials and art media while navigating both the remote and blended learning models in the face of a global pandemic. Artists have been encouraged to consider the resources and spaces that surround them as tools for creating while infusing elements of social justice and social-emotional learning into their art-making. Artists have developed a new artistic skillset that focuses on STEAM and technology in particular as an exciting, beneficial, and cutting edge pathway for creating. This years themes have included community, cooperation, activism, empowerment, imaginative thinking, and voice. It is our goal that scholars participate in a well rounded, inclusive, and culturally responsive art making experience based on guiding the whole individual at P.S. 274.

PS 84's arts program is a very comprehensive one following the Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. The arts are integrated in all the content areas using a variety of media and techniques. We are very fortunate to be a part of a community that is enriched with a variety of artists, galleries and studios. Our continuous collaboration with various arts residencies have enriched the arts educations of all our students. Additionally, we have partnered with cultural arts organizations to ensure that every grade K-8 is provided with instruction in the arts that is tailored to their developmental needs and interests. Our educators and partner arts organizations are evolving arts instruction to provide students with access to rich programming regardless of it being in-person or remote.

Performing Arts and Technology High School offers a varied experience in performing arts. Freshman year students take Introduction to the Performing Arts, where they receive a formal introduction to one of our arts disciplines (dance, drama, vocal music, and instrumental music), after an initial audition and placement process. Students then select a major in one of these four areas at the end of the freshman year. Sophomore year students study intermediate dance, drama, vocal or instrumental music. Students will begin their sequence of study in the major they selected at the end of 9th grade. Junior year students delve into advanced dance, drama, vocal music or instrumental music. Students will continue their studies in their chosen major. Senior year students attend an advanced studio in advanced dance, advanced drama, advanced vocal music, or advanced instrumental music. Students in the advanced studio will be engaged in development of professional portfolios and the creation of original pieces.

Our arts program has a number of important goals. We seek, as part of our focus on American studies, to expose students to the careful study of art and music history. We also provide students with the skills necessary to create meaningful works of art on their own. Finally, we place great emphasis on inculcating in our students an interest in seeing and thinking about gallery and museum exhibits, plays, operas, musicals, and other theatrical performances, contemporary film, and modern and classical dance.

q40_r1_c1_4: National Museum of African American History and Culture
q42_1_rev: The arts program at PS 223 provided instruction to students in dance, music, theater and visual arts through various media and repertoire. Students showcased their talents in these four disciplines by participating in virtual assemblies that focused on a different cultural theme each month. Our school partnered with arts organizations like CASA, the International Girls Ensemble and the STEAM-based Salvadori Center for both in-person and remote instruction in the arts.  Our visual arts teacher provided remote visual arts instruction to students working from home. Student artwork was showcased on Google Classroom, in the school building and will be celebrated in an upcoming virtual art exhibition. We are proud of our two students who were chosen for the PS Art 2021 exhibition as well as the four students selected for the Queens Borough Visual Arts Festival 2021. PS 223 was also excited to be a part of District 27’s Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month Celebration. The National Museum of African American History and Culture engaged our first graders through meaningful visual arts activities each week on “Joyful Fridays”. Families danced along with the Ajna Dance Company as they learned Indian Dance in a virtual setting.

Students at Lighthouse Elementary received remote arts instruction during extended learning time from two cultural organizations. Arts House provided guitar, dance, and fine arts. Take Two Film Academy provided visual arts and theater, which included classes in Puppetry; Character Creation; Becoming a You Tube Star; Animation; and Film Production, Acting, and Editing. In addition, Take Two Film Academy provided in-person arts instruction during the month of June.   Throughout the year, students had the opportunity to participate in the Annual Black History Month Show. Students also viewed a Black History Month production produced by Christian Cultural Center and The Lion King Experience produced by The NY Black Arts Festival.

PS 131 believes that looking, making, and responding to art is very important, particularly for our English Langauge Learners (ELL), our Students With Disabilities (SWD) and our general education population. We have a high percentage of ELL students (approximately 50%) and about 18% of our students have disabilities, and we see the arts as a safe place of expression outside of perceived limits allowing them to engage fully in the experience without being hindered by any inability they might feel. Often, the students most successful in the visual arts may not be able to communicate in English, but their creation gives them the tools for self-expression they may not find elsewhere. This feeling of success and self-expression can open a door to learning and allow them to grow in all subject areas. We have a close and long-standing relationship with our arts partners who all share our school’s philosophy.  Studio in a School and The Brooklyn Conservatory of Music have been working with our students for 20 + years.  This year we added Dancing Classrooms for ballroom dancing for our fourth graders and began an early childhood (PreK) pilot program with Museum of Modern Art (MoMA). Our goal is to provide a diverse menu of arts across disciplines and grades. The benefits that staff and students receive from these programs are immeasurable.

Like all schools across the country, our school has been significantly impacted by the Corona Virus. Our students, families, and our entire school community has felt its impact. The majority of our students and teachers have been in Remote Learning for more than a year, and we have worked collaboratively to ensure that our students received an effective, rigorous, and  standards based education. 

We are looking forward to returning to full time, in-person, sessions in September and continuing our partnership with Brooklyn Arts Council. Through this partnership our students were enrolled in classes that supported their Artistic and Musical expressions. We also want to explore other partnerships that would nurture our students artistic expression and curiosity.

We look forward to having our students participate in the Arts and build upon and support their resiliency, recognizing that for some of our students, they are returning to the school after being away for a year and a half. It is important that they have the capacity and ability to express themselves as they navigate away from remote learning and transition back to in person learning. 

We know that Art plays a powerful role in helping students to think creatively and critically, and look forward to supporting our students through the use of  Art, Dance, Music, and Theater.

Due to the pandemic, we were unable to provide in-house arts programming. However, we made up for that loss by partnering with vendors to bring the arts to life within our school building. Every month students were able to sing, dance, perform, and express themselves creatively. 

This year, we partnered with Midori and Friends with their Signature Series residency. Students made instruments and learned the history of jazz music and its origin. Musical IQ took us on a musical tour around the world and Ajna Dance Company helped us celebrate and understand the importance of Holi. Students were able to dance and move with the help of Mr. Chris and even got to see a live theater performance of "The Movement" with Leap. Leap also allowed our classes to partake in a theater residency, Poetry in Motion, and our 5th-grade students participated in a Digital Photography residency as well. 

Change for Kids provided our 4th-grade students with a Studio in the Box residency and they created their own beats. CFK also provided our kindergarten & first-grade classes with Music & Movement. Music for Many introduced us to storytelling through song and our Dare to Draw Assembly was one that will be talked about forever. 

The arts were alive and well at PS 160Q and we will continue this work in the upcoming school year.

This school year, the arts program at P.S. 120 took place mostly online. We worked with small groups and created an enrichment club through Zoom. All remote students had weekly access to art through a YouTube channel we created where students could follow along with us at home. Teachers also used our YouTube channel in the classroom and substitute teachers used it as well, when students were in- person. We can proudly say that every remote student had access to the arts. For the few children that were in-person, access to the arts was with a certified visual arts instructor. For next year, we are hoping for all students to be fully in-person, so we can continue our arts program in a more hands-on way. In addition, the arts increases our students' language acquisition, as well as supports their writing skills. Students next year will also be exposed to the arts through sustainability projects led by the physical education teacher. Our remote and in-person arts program helps students grow socially and emotionally.

The arts program at the Bronx Academy of Letters has been expanded upon over recent years, and that growth is still in progress. Currently there is both a full-time visual arts teacher and a full-time theatre teacher, who teach classes in grades 7-12. 

Alongside these instructors we also have an Artist-in-Residence program; these four residents teach the following high school classes each day: Theater Production, Poetry, Journalism, and Music Production.

All students in grades 7 and 8 are in either a visual arts or theatre course; all students in grade 9 are in one of the above arts courses; the majority of students in grades 10-12 are in at least one of the above arts courses.

As a school, our Arts Department engages in a variety of productions and events each year. Twice per year there is a Night of the Arts, which includes performances and products from all of the above courses (and from students of all grades). Twice per year there are also theatre productions, including a full musical (recent productions include Hairspray and Grease). There are also Poetry Lounges, art shows, and a collaboration with The Moth that occur throughout the year.

Brooklyn High School of the Arts is Brooklyn's official arts school. A District 15 school located in downtown Brooklyn, it is the only fully screened arts school in the borough. The intensive arts curriculum prepares students for conservatory and higher education programs as well as careers in the arts. It boasts one of the most accomplished performing and visual arts programs in the City of New York. The vocal/instrumental music program ranks among the finest in New York and achieves top scores while performing at the highest level at state and city-wide competitions annually. The visual arts program routinely wins major distinctions and has been featured in galleries across the country. It is a pipeline to major art universities here in New York and nationally. The dance program features the finest instructors in NYC and supports dance students in receiving scholarships to college. The spring dance concerts are highlights to the entire community. The drama department features three main-stage productions and several smaller performances every year. They are regularly featured in the Schubert Theater Festival on Broadway. Students may also pursue musical or technical theater. As one of ten "Exploring the Arts/Tony Bennett" partner schools, Exploring the Arts (ETA) provides students with many opportunities for real world internships and professional residencies in the arts. Students graduate with a New York City Arts Endorsed Diploma along with their Regents and Advanced Regents Diploma

We relate visual arts and music to all curriculum areas to align with the Common Core Learning Standards. It is important for students to have an in-depth understanding of the formal elements of design which will be used in each project they work on. Students will learn to understand new ways of expressing themselves through various cultures and techniques. More importantly, the children should develop a sense of achievement. Achievement installs confidence which raises self-esteem.This is what teaching is all about!

Lou Gehrig Academy (LGA) believes in nurturing the talents of students by creating an arts enriched environment. Through the arts, we aim to inspire students to be critical thinkers, keen observers of detail, lifelong arts learners, makers and appreciators of the arts. Aligned with the New York State Standards for the Arts, and the NYCDOE Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts, LGA exercises a rigorous approach to teaching the arts. Together with partner cultural organizations, we bring equitable high-quality arts education to all students, offering them the opportunity to engage in meaningful art experiences, and relevant discourse with each other about the arts.

At Public School 186Q (Castlewood) we follow a balanced arts program that aligns with the NYC Blueprints for the Arts, State Standards and National Standards for Music, Theater and Visual Arts. Our visual arts program introduces mentor artists and studies their work to teach elements of art and principles of design. Students are exposed to various media and interdisciplinary approaches. Examples of student work are displayed throughout the school building all year long. All students participate in core music classes. Through singing, playing instruments, movement, listening to music, and various other activities, students receive instruction to help them reach their fullest potential both musically and educationally. Also, in addition to core music classes, we offer a variety of in-school ensembles and enrichment opportunities. Students engage in educational theater practices which explores upon all elements of theater-making. This includes performing, directing, playwriting, history, performance analysis and technical theater (scenery, props, costume, lighting etc).

The goal for Olympus Academy this school year was to form a school band and to give more opportunity for students to learn to play musical instruments.  Due to COVID, this goalhas been postponed until next school year. We have attained additional instruments so that students will have more options.  In addition, we hope to help students become more familiar with using music software to create beats and song tracks.  Students will continue to be exposed to both the theory and practical application of the arts.  We continue to give students the opportunity to attend arts programs and performances outside of school and to encourage participation in the All-City High School Music Program.

The goal of the visual arts program at Helen M. Marshall School is to create experiences in which students create and assess their own work, analyze masterworks and conduct peer critiques. They learn the elements of art and principles of design, college and career options and acquire the necessary vocabulary to discuss art. Students explore a wide range of materials and techniques. The goal of the music program is that students will develop the necessary skills to create, discuss and analyze music. They study the basic structure of music and become familiar with different styles and their historical context.

Visual arts and music are offered to all students in compliance with NYS graduation requirements. The visual arts program includes studio art and art history, with an introduction to artists and artwork with a global perspective. Students experience creativity as a means of expression through an understanding and application of the Elements of Art and Principles of Design with culminating exhibitions. The music program offers students a hands-on experience of music creation: making beats, sampling, writing melodies and chord progression, and song construction. Students also learn the different genres of music and learn the history of American musical forms. Programs are aligned with NYS and NYC Standards in The Arts. Our staff is committed to offering students a variety of experiences in the arts, including off-site visits to museums, cultural events, and performances throughout the year. Student and staff theater productions and events are developed and produced in-house during the school year. Also offered is Stage Craft, a theater elective class, where students collaborate on multiple-devised performances and presentations. College level visual arts courses are available to students for college credit through La Guardia Community College and the College Board programs, both on the High School for Health Profesions and Human Services campus.

During the 2020-2021 school year, MFTA worked with our school, and we were able to have "live" sessions on Wednesdays, which focused on music and arts. Students and families participated across our 5 sites during this hour. We were also able to plant a school garden and grow microgreens in classrooms, which also influenced the content of students' art work painted with water colors.

Nathaniel Hawthorne Middle School 74 provides rigorous arts instruction across seven different arts disciplines. As part of our individualized approach during the 2020-21 school year, our students were provided with individual choice and could choose: Instrumental music, vocal music, graphic art and design, studio art, theater, or moving image. We continue to provide additional arts learning through our collaborations with World Dance Theatre (Cultural Dance Project), Arts Horizons, Jose Limon Dance Company, Jazz at Lincoln Center, Music Memory, The Museum of the Moving Image, and the New York Historical Society. Our Dance program was part of Arts Achieve over a eight-year period, which created a foundation for our teachers and students to learn how to use peer and self-assessment to drive instruction. Our teacher team has shared these best practices, and this approach has been shared across the Arts Department. Three of our arts teachers were facilitators this year during Arts Monday professional development, and three of our other arts teachers participated in these professional development opportunities. Their work and research focused on utilizing different types of formative assessment in order to guide instruction.

At I.S. 237, we strongly believe students involved in the arts make gains in math, reading, cognitive ability, critical thinking, and verbal skills. Our school's theme is "The Arts", therefore careful attention is given to planning lessons and projects to ensure that our magnet theme continues to flourish. We are fortunate to offer our students both performing and visual arts classes during the school day as well as an extensive afterschool talent enrichment program.

At P.S. 346 Abe Stark, we have a K-5 music program in our school. All students, regardless of learning modality, received music instruction in keyboard with the Music and the Brain curriculum this year.

P.S. 58 The School of Heroes strives to provide all students with the chance to participate in visual arts, music, theater, and dance programs in compliance with the NYS Blueprints for Arts. Students in grades Pre-K -6 receive music, visual arts, theater, and dance instruction on a weekly basis from both full-time school-based arts teachers and their classroom teachers, who further enhance their classroom arts curriculum through drama lessons. Students present their culminating projects in visual arts, music, dance, and drama through classroom projects, online presentations and bulletin board displays throughout the year. P.S.58 follows the Music and the Brain program, which incorporates music history, music literacy and keyboard.

ISLA's Studio Art program offers a foundation for advanced courses in art such as Pre- AP & AP courses that are offered in high school. This satisfies the Art graduation requirement.
Beginning in middle school there is an emphasis placed on understanding the Elements of Art and Principles of Design as a basis for learning about and building artistic skills. Students will explore a variety of artists, art processes and materials such as drawing, painting, printmaking, two & three-dimensional design. Student artwork will reflect aesthetics & cultural and historical contexts. Current topics and themes are introduced to build student interest/relatability as well as a tool to teach and reach across the curriculum.
Willingness to get involved in the creative process is a more important requirement than the student’s talent or previous experience.

At the Urban Assembly School for Careers in Sports, all our ninth grade students are required to take a visual arts class where they create paintings, sketches and masks. Our students in grades nine through twelve also have the opportunity to participate in other arts-related activities such as theatre presentations, spoken-word evenings, and script and novel writing. This year we had Vivo Flamenco dance residency.
This Year due to Online learning we worked mostly on graphic design using online applications.

PS 196 is an elementary school that firmly believes that the inclusion of Arts related instruction does have a significant influence in the overall well being in matters pertaining to childhood development. Our goal is to use the arts as a method of heightening student's abilities to both express themselves in a creative and socially acceptable manner, as well as to bring greater levels of student appreciation to all art related mediums.
The arts harbor a sense of value and accomplishment. The arts help foster an individual sense of identity which in turn helps a student develop as an individual. The arts help students to make decision as well as problem solve.

The Visual Arts Program at PSMS 124 follows the Blueprint for Teaching and Learning in the Visual Arts. Through the five activity strands, students are offered a comprehensive and multifaceted set of visual arts-related experiences. Formative assessment is utilized in the arts classroom to support students and improve performance. PS/MS 124 will continue to enter art competitions such as the Queens Borough Arts Festival, the Ezra Keats Bookmaking Contest, and PSART.  In the graphic arts, students are encouraged to develop an interest in the field of graphic design. They develop their digital skills by creating a complex piece of artwork using Adobe Photoshop Elements. The program enables students to create, edit, organize and share images with the use of a computer.  The Dance/Creative Movement program at PS/MS 124 emphasizes building a foundation of dynamics of movement with the incorporation of spatial awareness, use of effort, shapes and relationships between the dancers. As students move to the middle school level, there is the opportunity to work collaboratively with their peers in dance-making, aligning the learning process with the Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in Dance.  The music curriculum concentrates on thematic areas of study, including multi-cultural songs, content area music, holidays, celebrations, and social music. Various composers and musicians are also studied. Students engage in choral singing as well as write lyrics and create their own verses to songs.

This year, we maintained our arts teaching staff of two certified art teachers and expanded our art department by adding a third certified art teacher who will focus on developing our work based learning curriculum for all of our students. Students at The Urban Assembly School of Design and Construction have the choice of taking two distinct pathways in visual arts. One pathway leads to a certification in Architecture and one leads to an Arts Endorsed diploma in Fine Arts. To help students make this choice, all entering freshmen take a year-long Foundations course which introduces them to the visual vocabulary and skills of art and design. Students then choose which pathway is right for them. Over the next three years, students will then have art or design every day and will engage in a variety of 2D and 3D projects. Our school maintains an active design studio, an art and sculpture facility with ceramic kiln, and a fabrication lab with 3D printers, a CNC router, and a laser cutter. As part of their chosen pathway, students will also participate in a variety of career discovery activities. These include job site visits, guest speakers, and afterschool internships. Twice a year students in both pathways present their work to a panel of arts professionals and contractors.  During the pandemic, arts students focused primarily on digital media and architecture.  In this new virtual setting, students were also able to learn from artists and designers from around the world.

During this challenging year, the arts and classroom teachers worked diligently to provide P.S. 230 students with a strong arts program. 

Staffing and programming changed multiple times this year.  Some students participated in fully remote instruction.   Other students were blended remote, and later in the year many students were able to return in person full time. 

Students learning remotely participated in visual arts weekly, and some grades had music.  Many in person classes received music education with our music teacher.  Classroom teachers often did music activities with their students too.  Dance was provided both remotely and in person by our music, physical education, and classroom teachers.  Visual arts was not provided in person this year, but students engaged in art with their classroom teachers. Some grades participated in outside remote arts residencies.

Our younger students participated in Community Through Music with Suzi Shelton.  These virtual sessions were enjoyed by both remote and in person students.

Fifth grade continued their tradition of an end of the year talent show. This year it was virtual.

Our school came together to prioritize the arts to empower our students through the arts.

The Visual Arts Program this year shifted to a full remote learning platform. Artists were exposed to new art making media such as digital art, photography, photo editing, advertisement, comic books and more. They were given opportunity to engage in learning through interactive platforms such as Nearpod, FlipGrid, Edupuzzle which enhanced their exposure to art history, art movements and feature artists. We utilized museum websites as a means of virtual field trips and exploration. Artists were exposed to art based career options and how to integrate technology into the visual arts world. Feedback was provided on a digitial platform using Jamboard and Padlet allowing artists to reflect on both peer and teacher feedback. Digital art allowed for more in-depth revision and process. Themes throughout the year integrated with the schoolwide literacy curriculum creating cross-curricular connections and establishing deeper content knowledge.

The Brooklyn Brownstone School offers both music and visual arts to all of its students two to three times a week. The goals of our arts program promote serious artistic study while also making inter-disciplinary connections to core subjects. We have aligned our instructional goals with the Common Core Standards and the Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. The visual arts program includes working with various kinds of materials, art history, and an afterschool art club for qualified students. The music program includes choral music, music history, music theory and instrumental music. We participate in Little Kids Rock creating student bands, giving meaningful experience to careers in music, and team building. This program includes learning how to play keyboard, music theory for beginners, experiencing a variety of musical styles, composing, and improvising. Opportunities to see students' artistic talents are available throughout the year. Community meetings with student performances are held twice a month. Student art is continually posted on the walls of our school. We also partner with Jazz at Lincoln Center's "Jazz for Young People", three interactive concerts that are well attended and two in-school student lead talent showcases as well as monthly musical performances aligned with our character building curriculum, "Heartwood". Musicians and artists visit from the community to provide instruction and information about careers in music. Activities reinforce commitment to lifelong learners.

Our arts program consists of an affiliation with Studio in a School for ART in 3k-K and Musical IQ (Musical IQ was postponed due to COVID, but we want to continue next year). Studio in a School fosters the creative and intellectual development of New York City youth through quality visual arts programs directed by arts professionals. The organization also collaborates with and develops the ability of those who provide or support arts programming and creative development for youth both in and outside of schools. At Public School 155, the residency is currently focused on our 3K - 1st graders. Musical IQ has partnered with us to serve our kindergarten through fifth grade students. The program curricula includes musical skills development and musical culture incorporating geography, history, and multiculturalism. Students experience the creative process and are a part of the making of a new musical creation learning self-reflection and discovery in the process. Through experiential learning, which is more naturally integrated than conventional study, the children experience a sense of community, teamwork, leadership and a tangible example of powerful collaboration.

Dos Puentes Elementary prides itself on its arts programming. We offer programming and activities in visual arts, music, dance and theater. There are at least four musical/ dance performances, two in-house gallery exhibits and many arts-related workshops and field trips each year. Visual arts is provided by Studio in a School and serves all our students weekly.  Children work with a teaching artist in Spanish to learn sculpture, drawing, painting, and printing. This is extended into the classroom during our daily 'Explorations' period. We have full-time, certified dance and music teachers who serve all our students. Children receive music classes weekly. They learn to sing, play the drum, recorder and ukelele and use other percussion, string and wind instruments. In dance, students learn creative movement, cultural dances, as well as contemporary modern and authentic jazz dance. Music is taught using the Orff model of teaching.
