Students embody music rhythms, experiment creating their own music as well. All arts programs are centered on collaboration and improvisation. As a dual language Spanish/English school, language and culture are reinforced through the arts. All classrooms also participate in our New Victory Theater partnership attending performances at the midtown theater. We offer students access to chorus, Capoeira, theater, the 'Just Dance' Team, Latin dance, jazz through residencies, partnerships and afterschool programs.

P.S. 236 Mill Basin, along with support from the Parents' Association, supports all modalities of art and it’s studies for all the students atour school. We have included art, dance and Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Math (STEAM) as parts of the school curriculum. Supplemental residences and experiences in the areas of music and theater round out the experiences and direct instruction the students receive. We continue with our development of clubs and student choice for these activities, so students receive as many experiences in the arts as possible. Limited school funding is supplemented by the generous support of the Parents Association and local, city and state funding. We continue in our efforts to provide students with a full, well-rounded education with as many supplemental experiences as possible, ensuring that students partake in the arts and all that New York City has to offer.

The PS 163 arts programs are focused on developing students’ artistic learning in order for each student to learn and to succeed to their own highest levels of achievement. Students engage in learning and projects that are focused on the skills and standards addressed in the NYCDOE Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts and the NYS Learning Standards for the Arts. Our lessons are used to teach, encourage, and expand our students’ creative and critical thinking skills. Students are able to explore a wide variety of visual arts and music techniques and materials while they develop skills in self expression and become confident learners. Students self assess, peer assess, critique, and refine their work. They are encouraged to share ideas and work on assignments that entail research, collaboration and cooperative learning. Through the arts, students learn to respect and appreciate multicultural ideas by gaining an understanding of the vital role the arts play in societies and cultures around the world. Our 2021 PS 163 Art Expo was presented virtually and shared with our community. Students' works were promoted through exhibition and submissions to numerous art competitions this year. Two of our students won positions at the Bronx Borough Arts Festival and one student placed as a semi-finalist in the PS Art competition. Arts teachers engaged students in relevant and engaging learning during both live and remote sessions this year as the arts remain a vital educational focus for our school.
The Public School 277 school community continues to do its best to provide our scholars with as many arts-related experiences as possible.

We provide music instruction through the Noel Pointer Strings Program. We have an F- Status music teacher who provides instruction to students weekly. Students view and participate in monthly assembly programs written and produced by the teachers. Students in music programs participate in concerts as well. Our students have the opportunity to sing/compete at the Music Memory Program yearly.
We also have Keys 4 Success Piano instruction. Students are learning how to play the piano during weekly instructional lessons.

Even while arts have been remote this year, PS 249 strives to enrich student learning by aligning the arts curriculum with the national, state, and city standards. We continue to support student independence, content knowledge, and the ability to think critically. Students in PS 249's arts program are encouraged to engage fully in the art-making process at home this year, taking creative risks and developing their own voices. Throughout the school year, young artists exchange feedback, make revisions, virtually display and perform their work as well as share in artful experiences with their families and community. The arts team continues to work collaboratively with administration. Professional development opportunities make sure lessons are supported by the NYCDOE Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts and stand behind the mission of PS 249 which is to nurture students as they become college and career ready.

PS 106 has rooms, supplies and teachers dedicated to music, theater and visual arts. Students are taught arts based on National Core Arts Standards and NYC’s Blueprint for Teaching and Learning the Arts. We, at PS 106, believe that the arts support academic growth, equips students with various ways to express themselves, and builds confidence, all while opening doors to culture and history. Our students have competed in ballroom dance, created art with the Park Avenue Armory and, each year, students and teachers proudly work in collaboration with the school community, to produce a performance. Students act, sing, dance, create sets, work lighting, sound and stage. Students do what they didn’t know they could do using artistic expression, professionalism and camaraderie. 
This was not a normal school year. Despite not having an art program this year, teachers at PS 106 worked to incorporate the arts into their curriculum, whether it was learning history through cultural music and dance, acting out a play in reading group, or devoting time to guided drawing lessons. Many teachers found new ways to connect with their students through the arts. Some connecting by discussing art on a virtual museum tour, others by creating art together from a YouTube video. While we anticipate a return to our arts program with much hope in the coming school year, we at PS 106 will carry this experience with us and remember the true value of the arts and its influence on how our students learn.

Arts programming at P.S. 150 Christopher is provided by different community-based organizations and is funded by a Violence Prevention Grant (SVEVP). Programming is based on a specific number of scholars. Next year, the school community is looking into providing scholars with an African dance and visual arts program that will also address scholars’ social and emotional needs. All the scholars will experience the arts by a certified arts teachers. We will apply for grants to support this initiative in the school community.

Public School 273 serves Pre-K through Grade 5 scholars. We believe that providing a quality arts program (including, visual arts, music, and theater education) is integral to addressing the needs of the whole child.  Our visual arts program serves all of our scholars and is integrated and sequential. It supports individual interpretation of ideas and feelings while providing opportunities for experimentation in a variety of media (painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, and sculpture). In Pre-K through Grade 5, our theater instruction teaches empathy, creates strong communicators, builds teamwork and collaboration, relieves stress, and promotes creative thinking and problem solving. In Grades Pre-K through 4, our music teacher implements differentiated instruction and builds upon the strengths and challenges of multi-cultural, multi-lingual, and multi-racial groups of scholars. She teaches instrumental music to Grades K-2 (including keyboarding in collaboration with the Music and the Brain program). For the 5th consecutive year, we received a grant from the Carnegie Hall Weill Music Institute Link up Program to provide great musical experiences for our Grade 4 scholars utilizing recorders, including our chorus.

Whitelaw Reid Academy of Art and Business (WRAAB) arts programs are at the heart of our unwavering commitment to excellence and equity for all WRAABsters.  Students learn to discover their artistic identities through hands-on learning experiences in three art forms.  In drama, dance and visual arts, students will meet and exceed grade level standards as they express their unique talents and voice as well as collaborate with peers to create artwork that will be seen and celebrated by our community.  Every student will feel valued as an individual artist who can make special contributions within our creative arts programs.

The Maxine Greene High School for Imaginative Inquiry (MGHS) is a learning community in which deep engagement with works of art enhances the imaginative capacity leading to the intellectual rigor of all students. This approach to inquiry based learning is rooted in the philosophy of Dr. Maxine Greene, which fosters a sense of self-worth, curiosity and empathy. MGHS empowers this diverse community to work towards a more just, humane and vibrant world. Teams of teachers currently work on shared inquiry around instructional practice as related to the integration of the arts across the curriculum.

Our classroom teachers integrated the arts into the academic curriculum. Additionally, PS 375 partnered with MoCADA Art Museum to provide virtual afterschool enrichment. 0ur visual arts teacher also provided visual arts programming both remotely and in-person after school 3 days per week. Our school community is looking forward to a renewed emphasis on arts education and enrichment. We are also planning to partner with arts organizations in dance and music to compliment our visual arts program.

High School of Applied Communication’s visual arts program features project-based learning for students in a range of traditional and digital media. Students learn about the real-world context for art and design and develop the ability to self-reflect and provide meaningful feedback to their peers in a critique setting. Students are exposed to various professions in the art and design fields and develop an understanding of how art and design permeate many aspects of daily life. Along with gaining proficiency in traditional visual arts media, such as painting, printmaking, and observational drawing, students have the opportunity harness their skills in digital media, learning photo editing, vector graphics, and web design. Students may even further increase their college and career readiness by opting for certification in Adobe Creative Suite and Microsoft Office. For the 2021-22 school year, we are committed to bridging the gap between print and digital media, exploring mixed media projects that allow students to combine analog and digital techniques.

The High School of Computers and Technology combines modern technology with visual arts to align with our technology based curriculum and meet the cross-curriculum needs of our students. This includes concepts such as photo editing software and platforms, block-coding animations, website design, 3D modeling, and additive manufacturing.

PS 133 is committed to quality education in the performing and visual arts. Our dedicated dance studio features mirrors, flooring, barres and technology. Lower grades focus on creative dance as well as an intro to ballet technique, choreography and dance history. Upper grades begin with an intro to dance covering creative movement concepts and then focus on ballet and modern technique, Jazz and Hip hop dance history, and choreography. In our drama program students develop social and emotional skills, as well as creative thinking skills. They develop performance skills focused on using ""The Actor's Toolbox"" - the body, voice, and imagination. Units of study include pantomime, playwriting, scene study, and puppetry, among others. The STUDIO visual arts program is a dedicated art studio where the students are encouraged to experiment in a variety of styles including drawing, painting, printmaking, collage, sculpture, 2-D applied design, and media tech are integrated into classroom content. Our cultural partners provide new and exciting opportunities for our students to express themselves, in addition to providing opportunities to interact with artists and arts venues in our community.

Due to scheduling requirements related to COVID-19, it was necessary for our music teacher to be placed in the classroom this year but will be returning to the music program for the 2021-2022 school year. We also plan to continue with residencies and field trips from years past.

P.S. 127 Mckinley Park offers a sequencial visual arts and dance program throughout the year. The students participate in hands-on activities in visual arts and learn about different artists and the history of art. The dance program teaches our students choregraphic movement based on various styles of dance for various performances. Our school offered a music enrichment afterschool program. The afterschool music enrichment program gave the students the opportunity to learn about vocal performance. Dance and theater are integrated in assembly programs and other content areas

This year Liberty Avenue Middle School added a full-time theater and music teacher bringing the school to three different full-time arts educators.  Thus, we will be adding instrumental music, performing arts, and theater to our students' instructional program in 2020-2021.

q40_r1_c1_3: Learning Through an Expanded Arts Program (LEAP)
q42_1_rev: Grant Avenue Elementary School is committed to the arts as a critical way in which our students learn more about the world and more about themselves. Typically, our students experience quality dance and music instruction throughout the school year with our specialty teachers. Students receive additional arts instruction from cultural organizations across the city, including Story Pirates and Musica Viva NY, thanks in large part to our partnership with Change for Kids. Even with the curricular changes brought about by remote and hybrid learning this school year, students PK-5 have had the opportunity to engage in regular music and visual arts instruction as well as theatre- and dance-based residencies both synchronously and asynchronously. We pride ourselves on engaging with parents through the arts, and together we celebrate our talented students and look forward to once again showcasing their work at annual musical performance events: concerts, dance recitals, a fifth grade musical and posted displays of student artworks throughout the year.

For this school year, students focused on learning the elements of music.  In doing this, they were enabled to understand any piece of music, whether through performance or analysis.
Sixth graders explore the world of music through the soprano recorder. Students start their instruction in reading standard music notation. Seventh and eighth graders begin to learn how to how to play the B-flat clarinet. They play music by reading musical notation. This year, many of our eighth-grade students received admissions to performing arts high schools.
A licensed art teacher teaches all students visual arts. Students studied the elements of visual arts and the work of famous artists, replicating techniques to demonstrate understanding, knowledge, and appreciation. Also, all students participating in the Extended Learning Program receive an opportunity to participate in visual art, dance, step, and theater, most of which are taught by teaching artists. By June 2022, more than 85% of the students will achieve a score of 80% as measured by the New York City Blueprint for the Arts.

Public School 54 provides visual arts, poetry, music and film to many of our students both in person and remotely.  However, COVID restrictions have put limitations on our abilities to reach out to cultural organizations.  The arts have been implemented through the school’s staff.  We continue to celebrate our students’ accomplishments with visual arts exhibitions, film screenings and modes of expression to promote social change with our entire school community to promote the concept of a Violence Free World. Visiting museums have been done virtually through virtual field trips on Google Meet.  Two of our students exhibited artwork in the 2020 Bronx Borough-Wide Annual Visual Arts Virtual Festival which will be virtual once again this year.  One of our 3rd grade teachers provide music instruction in connection to the lessons taught.  Connections are continuously made with the core subjects to support learning through the arts.

Public School 135's arts program includes instruction in visual arts, music and drama. The arts are integrated into the school day via cluster programs, cultural arts organizations partnerships and teacher led instruction. Teachers integrate the arts with other subject areas such as English Language Arts, Social Studies and Science to provide students with learning opportunities that engage all their learning styles. We feel that it is important to expose our students to the world of the creative arts to engage them as lifelong learners and develop all of their abilities. Public School 135 values the arts in education and we are always looking for opportunities to expand our arts programs for our students.
P.S. 134 offers a range of arts opportunities for all students. The students take visual arts and music classes, and take part in art, dance, and theatre residencies

We nurture a school culture that is committed to our students’ creativity and their thoughtful, reflective participation in the community. Our Arts Program offers differentiated access for all students; after two digital visual art courses, we offer Graphic Design courses to strengthen their perception. We have an Art Club during the student lunch period as well as an after school program to provide greater access to studio time for each student. We also have a cheer leading (Dance) club, a guitar club, an anime club, and a video club.  

 Our students create high level work and participate in gallery exhibitions for example the Bronx Borough Art Exhibition at Lehman College.
 

The Parents’ Association enjoys art-making experiences and workshops.

q40_r1_c1_3: Learning Through an Expanded Arts Program (LEAP)
q42_1_rev: Lower Manhattan Arts Academy (LoMA) is dedicated to nurturing the artist in all students. Students take introductory classes in music, dance, drama and visual arts before committing to a three-year major in one of the disciplines. LoMA offers an arts endorsement pathway for students. Students receive in-house arts instruction and are exposed to a wide variety of cultural institutions and community partnerships within the arts. In addition to working with full-time certified arts teachers, our students work with a wide variety of teaching artists in their arts and academic classes. Students at LoMA regularly attend theater, music and dance performances as well as visit museums and cultural institutions. They have numerous opportunities to perform, direct and choreograph, including events such as our fall drama, spring musical, talent show and the Majors’ performance. Students at LoMA have a wide range of arts experiences incorporated into their daily academic classes as well as a wide range of extracurricular arts opportunities from which to choose.

At I. S. 25 Adrien Block, our arts program enables our students to create and perform dance, learn an instrument or sing in our chorus, while developing the various skills in multiple media and understanding the techniques required to express artistic vision.

Renaissance High School (RHS) offers courses in vocal music, instrumental music, theater and visual arts. RHS produced virtual showcases and films in lieu of live performance. RHS has a Beginning and Advanced Band, Beginning Piano, Beginning and Advanced Choir, Beginning, Intermediate, and Advanced Theatre ensembles, Beginning and Advanced Studio Art, all of whom were featured in virtual events like the winter and spring showcase and many events throughout the local community and the greater New York City area.

At P.S. 245, there is one full-time visual arts teacher and  one full-time music teacher. The students receive approximately 90 minutes of each discipline per week. Students are encouraged to explore and discover all aspects of the arts at this magnate school. Although there is no full-time dance teacher, many of the general education teachers encourage dance and costume making for many of the concerts and ceremonies throughout the school year. The visual arts teacher teaches sculpture, painting, printmaking, collage, drawing, and other construction units. We are confident next year will be very productive and we will get back to great art-making.

At P.S. 32 State Street, we recognize that the study of the arts enriches students' learning and their lives. Our program enhances students' abilities to express themselves creatively, supporting student agency, by offering opportunities to participate in a comprehensive integrated arts education. This includes experiences in school, as well as experiences in the community and New York City in general. Our program enables our children to reach the NYS Learning Standards in the Arts. The goals of the program are that children are actively engaged in creating, performing and participating in the arts, make use of available materials and resources, respond thoughtfully to a variety of works, and understand the cultural contributions of the arts.

We strongly believe that the arts should be an important part of a school's academic program. We have participated in and developed a wide variety of educational programs and activities to support the inclusion of the arts (music, visual arts, dance and theater) in daily curriculum offerings to our students. Many community agencies support us, including Third Street Music School Settlement and Studio in a School. Visitors to PS 19 often comment on the extent to which the students are engaged with their work. We are particularly proud of our school's warm and sociable atmosphere and productive learning environment.
Brooklyn Theatre Arts High School provides theater and music instruction and has a partnership with Roundabout Theatre Company.

PS 307's Arts Department consists of music for PreK-5 and visual arts for PreK-5 in-person and fully remote.  PreK-5 grade students received both music and visual arts once a week.  Both music and visual arts have their own classrooms where the homeroom classes travel to those arts classrooms.  The music teacher and visual arts teacher collaborated for the Remote Holiday Show, Remote Beloved Community Celebration and social media.

P.S. 128 Bensonhurst continues to provide an enriching and diverse arts program for all students. We use the arts to engage our students in both their artistic and academic lives. We have two full-time arts teachers and our curriculum is enriched by collaborations with various cultural arts organizations. Not only do we continue to follow the NYC Blueprints for the Arts, but we have integrated these expectations into our content areas, aligning our units of study with the Common Core Learning Standards. All students receive arts experiences in visual arts, music, dance, and theater. Students are actively engaged in various meaningful activities that foster creative expression, discipline, collaboration, and self-awareness. We also integrate the arts into our afterschool program. We believe that all teachers are teachers of the arts. Arts education allows students to be creative and expressive as we educate the whole child and prepare him or her to become future leaders. Every year, we see improvements in motivation, concentration, confidence, and teamwork amongst our students across the grades. Every experience enhances arts learning, and opens our students' eyes to new ways of seeing dance, music, theater, and visual arts. The arts are vital to our school, and loved by all students, teachers, administration, and families!

Clara Barton High School's arts programs include courses in visual arts, drawing, ceramics, and music. All Clara Barton students are encouraged and programmed to take one term of a required visual arts class and one term of music. Students are then encouraged to take visual arts classes, such as ceramics, graphic arts, drawing or studio art, or participate in chorus. Students’ artwork is posted throughout the building and in display cases. Our music classes now include ukuleles, recorders and other instruments due to funds provided by the NYC Department of Education. Last school year, Clara Barton received a grant from the Brooklyn Academy of Music. Although we weren’t able to hold classes this year due to COVID-19 restrictions, we are planning on having it once again in 2021-22. Other students are involved in Opening Act theater classes virtually. We had several events where students' work is submitted to competitions or exhibitions in the DOE. This year we had two winners and their work will be displayed for all to see.  We look forward to expanding the arts even more in the coming years.

This year we were able to continue providing orchestra for our 4th and 5th grade students, both in person and remotely.  Music continues to be taught as a subject for both remote and in person students.  The music program continues to support students learning and development in music and in all areas.  
Our teachers use daily brain breaks (several times in one day) to promote dance and movement for all students in person and remote.  
We are partners with Inside Broadway.  They provide our 3rd and 4th grade students with opportunities to develop and enhance their theater skills. 
We also have In My Sistah's Steps which we teach 30 females the art of STEP dancing.

Middle School 88's art program's goal is to ensure that the arts enable our students to be agents of their learning and to ensure that they are given a multitude of opportunities to develop, craft, express, and share their voice. We believe that the arts truly benefit and support all of our diverse learners and provides them with many possibilities to understand all forms of literacy (digital, media, visual, data, news) and opportunities to express themselves through different art forms.
Students had music this year. All classes were taught remotely.

This year at Cypress Hills Collegiate Preparatory School,  art was done both remotely and in-person.  The art program was based on a video game design using Minecraft Education with a focus on combining visual arts skills and computer programming skills.  Units from the School of Interactive Arts that focused on using computer programming in art class were also integrated into the curriculum.     Minecraft: Education Edition is an open-world game that promotes creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving in an immersive environment where the only limit is your imagination. Minecraft: Education Edition helps prepare students for the future workplace, building skills like collaboration, communication, critical thinking and systems thinking. The open learning environment gives students the freedom to experiment, encouraging creative self-expression and problem solving.

Our school's arts program is multi-layered, multi-disciplined and provides our students with the abilities to be competitive with their peers throughout the city. Each year, it is our goal to align all of our subject areas in an effort to provide our students with seamless learning and inquiry. Our students are exposed to varied forms of art including visual arts, theater, dance, and music. Our in-house arts teachers, along with our art consultants, are innovative and seek to stay current with the trends and new discoveries within their disciplines. We take pride in how we align each grade with the arts. Each of our grades is assigned an art form according to their social studies curriculum. Our artists and classroom teachers collaboratively study the units and decide what the essential question and year's focus would be for the students across each grade. We provide our students with authentic art instruction which allows them to truly understand the art form that is being studied. Our students are provided with many opportunities to engage in trips which enhance their art awareness and make their learning real and alive. Our students are also provided with many opportunities to study the varied forms of arts, collaborate with their peers and their teachers, and then present their Type III products. They engage in varied in-house art exhibitions as well as exhibitions outside of the school on stage, in museums, and at dance competitions. We tap into their talents.

At P.S. 156 Waverly, grades PK-5 collaborate with dance and visual arts teachers, students, and parents, in order to integrate the arts into the general curriculum. First grade teachers work in partnership with parents, arts teachers and other staff members to teach about the African culture. Students produce a play script around the African culture with the guidance of the teachers. They acquire African words or sayings and they learn different African dances and hear African stories. As a concluding activity, students present a play and dance performance for the community and parents to enjoy. The second grade students learn about several artists and their paintings. The students are encouraged to create their own paintings. These paintings are presented as a culminating event, where parents and the community can come and participate. Third grade learns about the Latin culture. After learning about different dances and the cultural history of the dances, the students study the Flamenco dance. Fourth and fifth grade students participate in our chess program and college and career readiness exercises. As a school, teachers work across grades to ensure that the students are being exposed to and experiencing multiple opportunities to learn about the arts, especially for Hispanic Heritage and Black History Month. In addition, three classes participated in the creation of puppets to represent the experiences, music, and cultures of our diverse community.
Art is incorporated in to our curriculum, and we have an extra curricular art program.

We have three forms of the arts at Jean Nuzzi I.S. 10: dance, music, and visual arts.  Because we strongly recognize the importance of integrating the arts in our school, we continue to offer our students elective classes in dance, music, and visual arts throughout the grades.  We are hoping to collaborate with other outside organization such as Queens Theatre in the Park Grant.  We also have an afterschool chorus program and offer instrumental music in the morning. We also have a DJ Club afterschool this year. We would like to apply for more grants/funds to increase our arts staff and arts programs for the students. An afterschool instrumental program would be wonderful. At the end of every school year, we host a talent show for the students to showcase their artistic talents.

For the 2020-2021 school year, P.S. 214 Michael Friedsam continued our chorus for 3rd, 4th and 5th grade students virtually. Piano instruction was also provided to all in-person 2nd to 5th graders, with an extended Piano Club. Piano students engaged in activities that encourage communication, observation, replication and creation of music, dance, and movement within their classes. This year we were awarded the Midori & Friends dance residency grant from Councilwoman Diaz for grades Pre-Kindergarten and Kindergarten for music residencies. We partnered with Funikijam and I Have a Song in My Heart virtually, and celebrated with a virtual culminating online performance. As a school we have participated in the annual District 19 Arts Fair. Contingent upon funding for the 2021-2022 school year, we plan to provide more arts related programs, residencies, and experiences next year for all of our students.

The arts hold a prominent place at Hamilton Grange Middle School. We are committed to making the visual and digital arts as well as music, including choir and orchestra, dance, theater, our annual musical production, and spoken word slam poetry as part of our regular school day and afterschool programming. Our commitment to the arts is twofold: 1) we want students to find their passion while here at Hamilton Grange, and through it build the discipline and work ethic necessary to be successful in whatever endeavor they choose; and 2) we know that training in the arts is beneficial to the whole child.  Sustained learning in music and theater correlates strongly with higher achievement in both math and reading. Art studies and activities help keep high-risk dropout students to stay in school. New brain research shows that not only does music improve skills in math and reading, but it promotes creativity, social development, personality adjustment and self-worth. Students who study the arts are four times more likely to be recognized for academic achievement and three times more likely to be awarded for school attendance. We look forward to working with you!

q40_r1_c1_3: Flushing Town Hall (Flushing Council on Culture & the Arts)
q42_1_rev: At P.S. 22 Thomas Jefferson, students regularly engaged in their music and art lessons, once during their seven day cycle. Performances and assemblies became virtual, extending the invitation to not just our students but their whole family. Students and their family could engage from home in programs such as, dance, puppetry, storytelling, and crafts. We hope for next year that our academic setting can be adjusted to include more of our past programs, such as theater, arts partners, artists-in-residence, and more enrichment and afterschool programs.

At Intermediate School 232, the arts program started the school year in the right direction. The visual arts teacher makes each lesson fun and the kids enjoy it. All the art lesson are hands-on activities. After students are done with their art assignment/project, they get an opportunity to write about their process and share with their classmates.

All students at P.S. 26 are provided with a high-quality arts education inclusive of music, visual arts, theater and media arts. Within our arts program, our teachers build students’ arts skills and knowledge and promote self-expression, collaboration and analysis by engaging students in hands-on learning experiences and deep conversations about works of art. Our goal is to continue to engage students in sequential, rigorous and culturally responsive arts education that promotes student voice and expression through the integration of innovative technologies and use of enhanced materials and resources. Our aim is also to increase celebrations that highlight students’ artistic development by inviting our school community to celebrate student work, as well as participate in and attend performances showcasing the creativity and innovation of all learners.

Traditionally, visual arts classes are offered to both middle and high school students and our music and dance classes work towards a production at the end of the school year.  This year our arts teachers created interdisciplinary projects based on the content of the core subjects teachers while tekeeping in mind the limited materials our students had access to in their homes as well maintaining social distancing regulations in the classrooms.  The music department was able to acquire ukuleles for each of our 6th grade students. Both remote and blended and through the use of virtual classes, teahers taught them how to tune and play the instruments.  Our dance instructor utilizes Google Meet and Zoom to offer individual dance instruction.

At East New York Middle School of Excellence, our goal is to expose our students to the arts to build awareness of themselves and their culture. We offer students the opportunity to learn performance sign language with an infusion of dance and music to encourage them to speak "their truth." Most of our field trips are arts-based giving our students the opportunity to attend a variety of arts performances and events. Students are afforded the opportunity to attend operas at the Metropolitan Opera at Lincoln Center, performances at BAM and Broadway performances just to name a few. Additionally, our full-time music teacher engages our students with all forms of music throughout the year from African drumming to pop music. Additionally, our school is the proud recipient of a significant grant through the Matisse Foundation. This grant has afforded us the opportunity to partner with organizations such as BRIC to expand the range of arts programs we are able to bring to our scholars. Scholars now engage in offerings which include hip-hop , Afro-Caribbean dance, spoken word, urban street art, and African drumming. Our band plays at all of our school-based performances and activities as well as at venues around the city. In addition to a dedicated music room, our school has a dedicated dance studio. Lastly, East New York Middle School of Excellence has also partnered with VIP Online Academy to offer distance arts learning including tap-dance, graphic arts, and poetry/hip-hop development.

The High School For Excellence and Innovation (HSEI) offers students an opportunity to hone their art skills while developing a strong foundation in the arts. Advanced Placement Art History has been an interest to our students as they begin to establish college credits in art. CDOS Programs will be introduced to HSEI next year offering the students an amazing opportunity to gain career development skills and graduate with a CDOS credential.  All arts classes are aligned with the College Board and New York State Standards.

q40_r1_c1_4: Museum of the City of New York
q42_1_rev: This year has been a challenging year overall and especially for arts programs.  We were not able to participate in programs with our usual partnerships such as the National Dance Institute or the New York City Ballet or hold student concerts or art shows.  All music classes and most art classes were taught online via Zoom.  However, arts instruction is an integral part of the school day at our school.  In addition to continuing the school based arts programs which included instrumental instruction (concert band, recorder), chorus, general music and visual arts instruction, we were able to continue our partnerships with Carnegie Hall Corporation and the Manhattan School of Music Opera programs through virtual programs.

Through remote learning and in person instruction, the arts program at P.S. 128 The Lorraine Tuzzo, Juniper Valley Elementary School was aligned with the New York State Literacy Standards as well as the NYC Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. Students were able to work with a wide range of strategies to create traditional and contemporary works of art in a creative setting. Projects are completed in units, where students build upon prior-learned skills in visual arts, music, and theater.

Public School 91 has two certified music teachers who provide  general music instruction. All students in grades kindergarten through fourth grade receive music instruction at least one period a week. We have a certified visual arts teacher who provides instruction for most students in grades kindergarten through five for at least one period per week. In addition, we have a part-time dance teacher who works with grades K-5. Additionally, we have residency artists from Materials for the Arts who work with classroom teachers and students on culminating projects teaching art through socials studies content to students in grades 3 and 4. Art residents from Studio in a School provided visual arts lessons to classes in grades 2-5.  Afterschool programs met weekly and included visual arts (30). During remote learning, visual arts, dance and music instruction continued.

The RKA Arts Department has worked hard to strike a balanced approach in our middle school arts curriculum. As students move from sixth grade to seventh, we encourage them to commit to a two-year sequence in either visual arts, band or chorus during grades seven and eight. As sixth graders, they experience two half-year arts classes so they can make a more informed choice about the longer commitment. We are blessed with truly gifted arts teachers who provide rich classroom instruction. These teachers also provide authentic performance experiences at our Winter Arts Festival and our Spring Arts Festival. In high school, there are opportunities for Advanced Ceramics in our AP Ceramics class in addition to high school core art classes. We also offer a guitar class, Painting through History, and ceramics electives. We are proud of the array of arts experiences available to our students in grades six through twelve.

CMSP has the goal of exposing all students to various art disciplines. CMSP327 continues to make key investments in providing arts instruction to all 6-12 students. We have a  full-time a visual arts teacher and a full-time dance teachers. We have a part-time drama teacher and a part-time music teacher. CMSP made strategic schedule decisions to ensure that students would be exposed to at least one form of arts education during the hybrid school year: 6th grade Music, 7th grade Studio Art, and 8th grade Dance. Our drama program expanded beyond the two courses offered to also include multiple virtual plays, including our first bilingual play. We have also continued to lean on partnerships with our community based organization to ensure afterschool programs have arts instruction included.

At Public School 46Q, we value the importance of the arts for all of our students. We offer a multifaceted and comprehensive set of experiences in the arts through their integration in all subject areas. The school is decorated with student created art masterpieces. The performing arts are highlighted by the winter and spring concerts. Choral instruction is provided to all students in both lower and upper grades, and our children receive a variety of instrumental music instruction with band instruments including: piano, string instruments, keyboard, percussion, electric guitar and acoustic guitar. We have a Rock Star Band, junior and senior chorus and a string ensemble. Additionally, all third grade students receive recorder instruction. Dance instruction is given to all students who show an interest in learning more about Asian cultures and are highlighted in a school-wide Lunar New Year performance. Our visual arts teacher showcases our students’ work in our annual Arts Show and musical theater is offered to all the students as each class puts on a musical theater production. Additionally, we seek to provide our teachers with professional development during our arts cycles with teaching artists.

The Bronx Dance Academy provides a highly engaging art program, where students create works that correlate to our thematic units. Our focus is to provide our students with a platform where they can express their interpretations of proven artist structures, which are aligned to Career and College Readiness.

Students participate in a focused sequential arts program in Dance or in Visual Arts during their tenure at Bronx Dance Academy. Our arts teachers strive to engage all students in rich experiences aligned with the goals of the Blueprint for the Arts and NYS Arts Standards in creating, performing/ presenting, responding, and connecting.

The arts program at P.S.140 is designed to facilitate the development of the 'whole child'. Our nurturing interventions aligned to the Blueprint for Teaching and Learning in Visual Arts is tailored to ameliorating the physical, intellectual, emotional and social well-being of our students. Instructional delivery is standards-based, rigorous, and aimed at invoking and enhancing their innovation, individualism, self-reliance and self-confidence in a comfortable milieu. Our students take ownership of major art projects by playing a significant role in decorating and advertising for celebrations and special events. By inviting parents to participate in in-house art exhibitions and performances, it's our hope that their involvement will not only help to highlight the various art-related career opportunities available, but also to foster a lasting appreciation for the arts, whether it be as an artist, future audience member, or a patron. We intend to expand our artscompetitions with 'meaningful prizes' for making programs, posters/flyers and decorations for in-house events. And as always, increasing the number of museum trips will afford our students the following: more opportunities to personally interact with and analyze exemplary works of art; provide lifelong effects to the development of their impressionable psyche: and to emulate the strategies the ‘Masters’ used into their own work. We also plan on expanding our community outreach and make the arts omnipresent in our building.

Although SY 20-21 continued our collective experiences of pandemic and sociopolitical unrest, our beloved theater teacher successfully maintained the connection between our students, families, and staff and the world of professional theatre. Balancing blended and remote learning, students, parents, and staff were able to attend several virtual performances this year, and our theater teacher brought her colleagues, professional playwrights, actors, and producers to conduct virtual workshops with students. Students continued building choreography skills, deepening theater arts with distinct integration of technology, exploring all genres of the performing arts through virtual tours, classes, workshops, and talkbacks. Our year culminates with a schoolwide arts celebration of song, dance and theater to which our entire community is invited.

PS/MS 280 is a kindergarten through grade eight school with a total student population of 753. We have a full-time certified arts teacher for grades six through eight, a second full-time teacher to teach visual arts and music to our kindergarten through second grade students, and three part-time art teachers who teach grade three to five students. It is our goal for all students to be enriched in the arts as much as possible. Classroom teachers' support include all aspects of art, dance, theater, music and visual arts in their lessons by creating thematic units. Throughout the school year, we engaged the students in virtual workshops and performances  to enhance this curriculum.

PS 195 is committed to offering students a well-balanced arts education. Unfortunately, due to the ongoing pandemic, our ability to implement our usual in-person programs and performances have been halted. We plan to restart our in-person instrumental music, step dance and modern dance programs for the 2021-2022 school year. 
This year, the staff had to be creative and determined, so most arts programs were held virtually. We were able to continue our Step and dance programs virtually. In virtual music classes, students were introduced to singing, body percussion, and bucket drumming. Students also created original music and recorded vocal tracks using Soundtrap, an online professional recording studio. Younger students were also able to be creative online using Google's Song Maker and Shared Piano applications. The incredibox application introduced students to loops to create beatboxing songs.
In the visual arts, teachers partnered with the Future Arts Initiative to create social justice themed digital media blogs with both remote and in-person students. Students have a scheduled two hour Art Exhibit with FAI in June. 
Classroom teachers were also committed to incorporating the arts into their curriculum using online resources like Art Hub and Google Drawings where students created digital mosaics.
Every Friday, the entire school has fun at Club 195, where all in-person and virtual students participate in virtual dance classes. Student performances are TBD.

The arts are a priority at P.S. 58. We encourage collaborations between our visual arts teacher and classroom teachers to promote ways to engage students through the arts. We believe in encouraging the talents of the whole child and celebrating the arts in performance, art shows and competitions. During virtual learning, classroom teachers prepared students through song and dance for class performances. With assistance from Bronx Arts Ensemble, our choir is growing and is becoming more popular among the school.  Unfortunately due to the pandemic, the visual arts program was halted this year.  We expect to continue and expand our program next year.

At the High School for Health Careers and Sciences, we offer a rigorous arts program. Currently, we offer courses in studio arts and graphic design as well as Advanced Placement (AP) Studio Art 2D. In our studio arts, students are given a foundation in the Elements of Art and Principles of Design. Students view, discuss and create paintings, drawings and mixed media art works. Additionally, the students are exposed to art history of various cultures. In graphic design, students are exposed to Adobe System programs: PSCC and Illustrator, as well as IMovie. In AP Studio Art 2D, the students develop their own portfolios with any medium or tools they choose. In the new school year, we will be introducing a new theater arts program. In this, students will be exposed to introductory acting skills, improvisation, basic design, directing exercises and theater history. Students will have choices how to showcase the theatrical concepts learned. Our students are given the opportunity to explore the arts in museums and film, view Broadway and Off-Broadway shows and visit colleges with arts programs. We are currently working with community partners to find more programs to engage the students, including the development of more performance opportunities.

PS 12 continues to try to provide every student with a variety of arts experiences whether they take place on or off-site during the school day, afterschool, on the weekend, or school holiday. Our goal is to provide every PS 12 student with a broad sense of the arts. Many of our students do not leave the community. Therefore, it is imperative to us that every student attends concerts, goes to museums, and experiences live theater. It is also important to us that our students be able to create their own art through hands-on experiential sessions and working with actual artists so that they can share their experiences with our students. PS 12's administration and teachers believe that the more enrichment we can bring to our students, the more we follow our vision of educating the whole child. We want our students to experience the world beyond their community, yet realize the possibilities the arts can bring to their world within their homes and their lives.

P.S. 224 Hale A. Woodruff provides a robust, culturally responsive arts program. Prior to the pandemic, we strengthened our dance and music programs through our partnerships with Alvin Ailey and Asase Yaa. Currently, we have monthly art showcases. We also have monthly performances at our assemblies which honor the accomplishments of scholars. We have also infused the arts and computer-technology throughout our curriculum. Through our restorative practice program, scholars participate in  theater role-play which supports their social and emotional growth.

The P.S. 277 Gerritsen Beach arts program encompasses a range of all arts disciplines. Each child in the school prepares and participates in a theater assembly program, which includes instruction in theater, visual arts, dance, and music, culminating in a final performance. Pre-K prepares and participates in small performances, which include the Lunar New Year and Special Family Member Day. This year many of these event occurred virtually. P.S. 277 has full-time visual arts, theater and music cluster teachers, who work with all classes from Pre-K to 5th grade. Several artist residencies and workshops in theater, media, dance and visual arts are provided to our students through parent-funded cultural arts organizations and grants/partnerships with city and community organizations. These residencies and workshops are the result of a partnership with Marquis Studios, through Parents Association funding, a DOE Arts Partnership Grant and through Council funds. These partnerships afford us the opportunity to provide additional arts instruction for all of our students. We believe that arts instruction should be integrated into literacy, math, social studies and science for our students as we continue to develop the quality of arts instruction for all students.

The High School for Environmental Studies (HSES) provides students with opportunities to engage in the arts for all four years. As a theme-based school which focuses on developing environmental stewards, we are proud to be able to provide our students with a Common Core aligned, well-rounded education that places a strong value on an arts education. In addition to offering our students beginning and advanced courses in chorus, orchestra, band and theater, we also offer ceramics, painting and drawing, as well as dance courses through a partnership with Alvin Ailey Dance Foundation. HSES is a culturally rich community that enjoys a great deal of student involvement in our arts program. Our teachers are dedicated to providing our students with meaningful experiences and exposure to a wide array of art forms, including environmentally themed arts projects.

PS/MS 188 is dedicated to identifying and nurturing each student's talents. To accomplish this, we strive to secure funding for arts resources and opportunities for our students. Our 2020-21 arts partnerships included Third Street Music School Settlement, Society of the Educational Arts (SEA), Repertorio Espanol, and Henry Street Settlement (Abrons Art Center) during the school day.  Teaching artists from The Educational Alliance and Henry Street Settlement (Abrons Arts Center) provided arts instruction during our extended school day. Our Technology Media Arts/MakerSpace program and extended day program have been highlighted by the NYCDOE as part of its "Showcase School" initiative.  We believe the arts provide a unique entry point into academics, and as importantly, meaningful pathways to high school and beyond. Given this, we collaborate with our cultural arts partners to implement arts-infused curricula in core subject areas as well as skills-based arts instruction. We are proud to have received NYCDOE's ELL/SWD (English LanguageLearners/Students With Disabilities) arts grants for the past five years>  The first was in collaboration with Marquis Studios and currently in collaboration with Third Street Music School Settlement.

Vibrant arts instruction was present at P.S./ M.S. 219 Paul Klapper in all four disciplines with our school staff and cultural arts partners. Pre-K to grade 8 students had designated music and visual arts teachers who delivered weekly instruction that was inclusive and differentiated to meet the needs of all learners during in-person and virtual learning. Quaver, Art of ED, Soundtrap digital curriculum resources and technology tools were implemented to ensure teachers and students were able to engage in relevant and engaging instruction. Our students had access to 1-1 and small group support throughout the year and were celebrated for their creative contributions during the PS/MS 219 Art Show and Music Showcase. Our 1st and 5th graders participated in theater instruction with Inside Broadway, our 2nd and 3rd graders, a visual arts residency with Guggenheim Museum, and our 4th grade students worked on movement and dance through our partnership with Young Audiences of New York. Virtual field trips and family events were offered to our whole school community. Arts and culture and the alignment of both were highlighted through the integration of culturally responsive sustaining education practices at our school. We are committed to pursuing this initiative in the 2021-22 school year as well as continuing along our trajectory of providing excellent, highly engaging, and developmentally appropriate arts education that builds across grade bands and disciplines.
This school year we offered K-2 a music program; 3-5 a dance program and K-5 Computer Science.

The August Martin High School arts program is comprised of music (steel pan, keyboarding, drums) and visual arts (studio art, visual art, Advanced Placement art).  The arts are embedded in scholars programs starting in ninth grade and continue through scholars twelfth grade year.  Teachers use summative and formative assessment practices to give scholars the support they need to grow and learn.  In addition, we have a culinary arts Career and Technical Education (CTE) program which allows scholars beginning in grade ten to explore their passion for the art of cooking.

The Arthur Tappan School PS/MS 46 is a community school that provides all students with a world-class education. We strongly believe in offering a well-rounded curricula, which goes beyond academics and promotes the development of the whole child through STEAM related activities, arts and letters. We work seamlessly to integrate and support each scholar’s social-emotional development, their artistic talents, their physical abilities, and their academic strengths and needs into our programming. By partnering with the Carnegie Hall Foundation, our students have gained an appreciation for music education and understand the fundamentals of performing in an opera. Studio in a School (SIAS) is another organization that has supported the arts program at The Arthur Tappan School. SIAS has afforded our scholars an experience to exert their own creative expression through 2D and 3D representations. Field trip excursions are a complement to our rigorous curricula offering scholars a unique cultural learning experience outside of our school building and to connect to the lessons learned in the classroom.

P.S./I.S. 229 Dyker serves children in Pre-K through Grade 8. Early childhood students learn about the elements of music that include singing, instruments, and movement, incorporating the Kodaly and other methodologies. Upper grades have an opportunity to join the school band, string orchestra, jazz ensemble and chorus. Visual arts students are empowered with experiences that challenge, build knowledge and skills in the use of the various tools, techniques, and intellectual methods of creating art. Our goal is to provide a sequentially standards-based arts education, which builds an appreciation of various cultures, connects to other disciplines through participation in NYC cultural institutions, and makes known the varied available careers in the arts.

Our school community believes that exposure to the arts strengthens the brain's attention system which results in students further developing cognitive skills. Our schools's art program focuses on various arts discipline. We offer music, visual arts, dance, and theater. Our music program is a full time program that allows students in grade 3K-5 to develop cognitive functions that facilitates problem solving, logical reasoning, and conceptual tasks. The music program includes Music and the Brain. This program allows teachers to interconnect literacy with music. Our dance and theater program offers additional opportunities afterschool for students to develop collaborative skills, problem solving skills and enhance speaking, listening and comprehension skills. The program is facilitated by the Society of Educational Arts. The key element of this program is that it is bilingual and touches upon native language skills in an effort to enhance second language skills. The visual arts program is an in-house program facilitated by a staff member. Through visual arts, students develop an appreciation for the arts and their own creativity. They explore concepts that formulate higher thinking skills and expand their imagination and creativity. Our program this academic year was successful. This was evident in the projects and performances our students engaged in.

During the 2020/21 school year, our arts programming was significantly impacted. We are looking forward to continuing our comprehensive arts structure when it is safe to do so. Our cluster teachers include one visual arts teacher and one theater arts teacher. Every class in grades K-5 receives one period of instruction in each discipline. We also have a music program that is funded by the PTA. Students in every class receive instruction one period a week from our music teacher. Students in every grade visit arts organizations throughout the year. These community based organizations include the Brooklyn Museum, Chen Dance Center, CSI Center for the Arts, The Queens Museum and the Whitney Museum of American Art. We also have a ballroom dance residency program for our 5th grade students.

Students in high school grades were able to take one to two semesters of visual arts. Students worked on standards-aligned visual arts assignments to build their secondary school arts portfolios through painting, sculpture and graphic design. Third year students  were able to design independent study courses in the visual arts according to interest and school capacity. Some students in high school also received an independent arts study using whichever programs they wished.

q40_r1_c1_4: Paul Taylor's American Modern Dance Theatre
q42_1_rev: We strive to offer a wide array of artistic programming to our students. We believe that arts education is an integral part of the middle school experience because of the opportunities it provides to expand student engagement and encourage creativity in expression. Currently, we offer instruction in band, dance, piano, and visual arts. To offer this range of artistic options, we actively seek to bring in cultural organizations to supplement and expand our own in-school offerings. One of our greatest partnerships, the Park Avenue Armory, has afforded our students an extraordinary level of enrichment through its residency programs and student workshops. All our work around the arts culminates in large-scale school performances held three times a year. These performances bring together the various artistic disciplines in a celebration of the arts. In a poignant performance held each February in honor of Black History Month, our school community is able to see the fullest integration of the arts and core subjects, including English Language Arts and social studies. As a school community dedicated to increasing the exposure and learning our students gain from the arts, we look forward to future expansion and opportunities for our students to connect to and through the arts.

At Public School 63, our commitment to the arts is always growing. Since the 2010-2011 school year, full-time music and visual arts instruction by certified arts teachers has been offered to all grades. In visual arts classes, students explore a variety of two and three dimensional media and techniques. Additionally, they are exposed to a wide variety of artists both contemporary and throughout history as well as careers in the arts. Usually in music, all kindergarten through second grade students are given instruction in keyboard, reading music and vocals. As students move into the upper grades, they learn additional instruments, such as the recorder, violin, trumpet, and bucket drums. To enhance our arts program, we continue our theater partnership with Scripts to Stage, Young Storytellers in 5th grade. In the 2020-21 school year due to pandemic conditions, all music instruction was provided remotely and asynchronously. Visual arts instruction was provided as push-in for hybrid students and remotely and asynchronously for fully remote learners. Scripts to Stage was also provided remotely.

Students have the option of engaging in one of two four-year tracks: visual arts and theatre. The instructional focus is college and career readiness around these disciplines. A multitude of partnerships leverage the expertise in NYC for the benefit of our students.

We received a grant from Broadway Jr and were able to provide theater arts to our middle school students. We also partnered with Thrive Collective to bring the arts to our 6th grade students, both in-person and remote.

q40_r1_c1_3: Hostos Center for the Arts and Culture
q42_1_rev: As a sixth through twelfth grade secondary early college school, our arts program focuses on the visual and theater arts. We have an extensive, award-winning creative writing program that we use to fuel our drama program. We have many outside agencies providing arts support through in-school and afterschool programs. In addition, our students take college classes at Hostos Community College in the arts. The emphasis is on pushing students to explore and reach beyond their preconceived limitations.

On top of a curricular exploration of studio art provided in the 10th grade, Bronx Lab students have the opportunity to explore the arts through theater instruction with multidisciplinary theatrical projects in science, history, and English classes created in collaboration with EPIC Theatre Ensemble. Epic Theatre Ensemble is an organization comprised of artists and activists dedicated to making bold theatrical works on professional stages and in public schools that inspires dialogue about social, ethical, and political issues. Epic builds thoughtful citizenship in communities throughout NYC, modeling creative engagement with civic issues by commissioning, developing, and producing socially-minded theater and connecting these plays to schools and neighborhoods via innovative in-school, afterschool, and public performance programs. Epic accomplishes this mission by inspiring students to be creative and engaged citizens, presenting compelling topics that transform the way people think, and collaborating with artists, students, and thought leaders to produce plays about critical issues.

The arts program at Queens Technical High School aims to enrich the experience of all students by exposing them to a variety of techniques, culture, and art history. We encourage our students to express themselves creatively to promote educational and emotional growth through different courses in studio arts and graphic arts.

The STEM Institute of Manhattan will continue to provide visual arts instruction through art residencies provided by Arts Horizons, Learning Through an Expanded Arts Program (LeAp) and the Leadership Program. In collaboration with these organizations, STEM students receive regular instruction in visual arts, dance and theater. Students also perform a full length Broadway Jr. musical production annually. Additionally, Arts Horizons and Harlem School of the Arts provide students with instruction in the performing arts, including voice and dance. As part of our regular school schedule, Friday Fun Clubs enable students to explore many aspects of the arts, including photography, Latin dance, and crochet. All classroom teachers integrate art through the content areas so our students continue to explore, design and showcase their work in our corridors and classrooms.

At P.S. 091 Richard Arkwright, our goals for the coming school year are to continue to integrate the arts curriculum into our common core curriculum. We will continue to work with our current residensies which are the Marquis Studio, as well as Ping Chong and Company.  We are hoping to continue working with Dancing Classrooms for our fifth grade students this year. We have been very fortunate to bring these organizations to our students virtually through Google Meets and Zoom platforms, both during and after school hours. As restrictions are being lifted, we will encourage teachers to take field trips to the many cultural institutaions that NYC has to offer.  This will continue to enrich our curriculum and instructional programs throughout the school.

PS/MS 5X, students are creative individuals with unique voices and perspectives. They create and perform artistically while adopting real life practices and behaviors of true artists. 

They expand their expressive capabilities, work through challenges, articulate problems and solutions, gain domain specific vocabulary. They discover connections between the art they make, the art made by others and the world around them.

At P.S. 536 students receive weekly Dance and Visual Arts instruction.  

Students engage in Weekly Assemblies where they are exposed to diverse types of music and dance (i.e. salsa, tap, etc.).

Students in different grade levels experience dance residencies such as Bollywood Dance, Bangali Dance and Swing.

In-person students are able to experience learning Violin in our afterschool program.

We have a Career and Technical Education (CTE) approved graphic arts program. Twenty five percent of the students in our school are enrolled in that program. All other students take one year of visual arts, generally in ninth grade.

Arts education continues to be a part of the everyday experience of students at I.S. 392. Our students are provided a well-rounded education that includes a balance of academics and arts, both during the day and afterschool. Yearly, our commitment to the arts is highlighted through our residencies in ceramics, theater, photography, and poetry writing with resident artists. This year, although virtual, we provided violin classes, pottery, steel pan, dance and vocal classes.  Our theater students were able to perform a series of virtual monologues after watching various productions in class and receiving instruction from our drama teacher.  This year our students at I.S. 392 also had an opportunity to audition for a role in our virtual production of Broadway Jr.’s "Dear Edwina.” This is the fifth year with this program, and our students and staff work diligently to put on a production that is attended by neighboring schools, as well as our superintendent and elected officials. Broadway Jr. has allowed our students to sharpen their skills in vocal music and dance over the past three years. In addition, art students have worked to create virtual sets for the recording of our theatrical production. To incorporate art forms of diverse cultural groups, we have added steel pan, stilt-walking and costume design in our arts offerings.
The arts program at Science Skills Center High School is designed to provide all students with exposure to all aspects of the arts to develop their appreciation, knowledge, and skills in the arts.

J.H.S. 216 George J. Ryan is a community-based middle school. All sixth graders go through a full arts instruction assessment in visual arts, choral and instrumental music and dance. They are assessed for talent, and based on that assessment, students and parents are invited to participate in tracked arts talent for seventh and eighth grade. Arts talent students are groomed to create arts portfolios in their specific discipline in preparation for auditions in NYC specialized arts programs in high school. Many of our arts students are chosen to attend prestigious arts schools such as LaGuardia High School and Sinatra High School of the Arts. Others continue to take arts courses in their local or chosen high schools. Some form of the arts (Dance, Visual Arts, Music Instruction, Filmmaking, Digital Art) is available for seventh and eighth graders outside of the talent track.

The arts program at The Fairmont Neighborhood School has devoted serious dedication towards bringing in outside resources to our students this school year. We have continued partnerships with existing cultural arts organizations as well as formed new relationships and partnerships with other arts grants to enhance both arts instructional time for students, and professional development for designated arts teachers. Students have continued their studies with music, visual arts, and musical theater. Incorporating storytelling, acting, and choreography has been a significant element that has now been added to our arts curriculum. Because of these added components, students have another means to express themselves through various performance activities that musical theater can include. Overall, students have arts engagements that consist of singing, dancing, acting, instrument playing, and creating art through the use and application of critical skills and tools.

In order to provide our students with a strong foundation in the arts, all students participate in music and visual arts instruction. These programs support and enhance the classroom learning environment by aligning the New York State Standards for Learning in the Arts, NYCDOE Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts and the Common Core curricula. We believe that music and visual arts enrich and enhance individual learning and promote schoolwide progress in the basic skills of thinking, listening, speaking, reading and writing, while supporting our students' social and emotional growth. Our music program offers instruction in general music, string ensemble, piano, and chorus. All of our kindergarten and first grade students participate in MATB classes for two periods per week with a MATB trained and licensed music teacher providing instruction using keyboards. Our visual arts program integrates Common Core content enriching concept and knowledge and exposing students to experimentation with various forms of art media. We provide our students in grades three through five with the opportunity to participate in our afterschool sketch club with the goal of enhancing students' observational skills and develop their drawing abilities. This year our fifth grade students participated in our theater club, The Hamilton Club, where students performed an adapted version of the famous Broadway show.

By providing all students with high quality education, we not only prepare them for the work place but foster personal development and full-fledged citizenship as well. Our educated students will be able to comprehend our multicultural society and face the challenges of the future.  Our goal as an art educator goes beyond the training of better artists to focus on the education of responsible, well-educated people who participate actively in the creation of their world. Art education can achieve this goal by being intellectual demanding, teaching higher thinking skills, aesthetic values, abstract reasoning, and creative problem-solving. Because of the absence of absolute answers in the arts, participating in the creation of an artwork teaches students how to envision and set goals, determine a technique and exercise it, evaluate and solve problems.  Using arts to sharpen awareness, develop talent, boast self-esteem and provide a personal and meaningful purpose contributes to students’ emotional well-being and provides a positive influence for at-risk students. Arts education also provides special needs students with the tools to express and communicate within their disabilities.   The arts, which we are teaching, overlaps and reinforces learning in other subject areas by providing interdisciplinary experiences. Our arts curriculum is designed to provide a holistic understanding of the world, enhancing general education.  We focus on art as a tool of expression and communication.

Our incoming 9th grade students experience Dance, Visual Arts, and Cosmetology, in their freshmen year. They are welcomed to decide a major in freshmen year where they then pursue a sequence in that major that culminates in taking the NYC Arts-Endorsed Diploma or NYS Licensing Exam for that selected arts major.

At P.S.110, we have a music program, an art program and a Dancing Classrooms residency. The goal of the music program at P.S. 110 is to support students in Grades K-5 to become independent composers, performers and learners of music. We use Orff pedagogy, where students learn music as they would learn a new language, and the theories and resources from Little Kids Rock to achieve this goal. The goal of the visual arts program at P.S.110 is to support students in grades K-2 to become creative artists. The students learn about artists throughout history by learning how to use art tools and techniques. The students follow the standards in the NYC Blueprints for the Arts.  At P.S, 110, we also have Dancing Classrooms as a residency for our fifth graders. Students learn and practice different traditional dances from all over the world. We want to open our students' minds and allow them to channel their inner creativity. At P.S.110, the arts are valued highly and we strive to to incorporate art into instruction wherever we can.

By June 2022, pre-k through grade five students at P.S. 188 Kingsbury will have connected the arts to personal experience, community and society through developing dance, music, visual arts, and theater literacy as measured by the New York City Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts theater benchmarks.

We are proud of the varied arts programs that our students woud normally participate in throughout the school year. With the generous assistance of the Parents Association and the participation of our arts committees (comprised of parents and teachers), we hope to be able to continue to offer these wonderful programs in the upcoming school year. PS 158 is committed to providing diverse instruction in the arts. We were so fortunate to have previously enjoyed diverse performances in school as well as many field trips.

Middle School 181 is committed to the development of appreciation of the arts in all students. The arts program endeavors to provide a comprehensive, standards based approach to the teaching of music, drama, and fine arts. We strive to have all students develop an appreciation for the arts as well as foster an understanding of cultural perspectives and contributions. Students explore the arts through constructive critiques, performances, projects and activities. Middle School 181 is enhancing its music and visual arts program to better prepare students for opportunities in high school and beyond.

We currently have an Arts Leadership Team comprised of students, teachers, and administrators. The Team works towards our Arts Mission Statement and goals set earlier in the year. They organize pro around the Arts. We highlight teacher strengths in the Arts, even if they are not certified as arts teachers. Teachers take these strengths and create programs during and after school, in addition to sharing environment consists of an Art gallery, "The Belmont Art Gallery', located in a hallway/bridge where all grades and programs are represented. Hallways, bulletin boards, and classrooms also come alive w partners, particularly DreamYard, who have assisted in deepening the work around the arts disciplines.

In spite of the pandemic, we were able to provide arts instruction this year virtually with our Arts partners. We were also able to celebrate and share our Black History Celebration virtually via a pre-recorded video.
Due to budgetary and staffing issues, PS 382 does not have a viable arts program.

The ultimate goal of our school arts program is to provide all students with an increased understanding of arts history and how art is used to express our feelings and beliefs. Students will learn to compare diverse art forms and develop a respect for the arts. In addition, students will discover, develop and enhance their personal abilities. The arts program at Public School 176Q is comprised of music, performing arts and visual arts. We strive to provide our students with quality music, dance and visual arts programs to develop young minds and build character.
