Our program includes but is not limited to: Chorus, Band, Piano, Drama, Dance and Conceptual Art. We set high standards and provide challenges that foster discipline and self-esteem because we believe the arts program is the heartbeat of our soul. It aids in the development and control of emotions while enhancing scholar’s creativity.

At Mathematics, Science Research and Technology High School, the Arts Program has been integrated into the core curriculum. Teachers are planning integrated lessons with our art, dance and music teachers. Students are exposed to different forms of arts such as Dance, Music, Visual Art and Theater. Due to the Covid-19 Pandemic students were not able to attend in person performances therefore our arts department created virtual performances in celebration of various holidays and events such as African American Heritage and woman's history month. Through these virtual experiences, students were still able to make connections with the socio-cultural and historical significance of theater and all the aspects of the arts including film and editing. This year, Mathematics, Science Research and Technology High School’s goals are to continue to integrate the arts into all content areas and create partnerships with various arts organizations to enrich the culture of our students so that students are able to express themselves through the arts and build their skills and knowledge in a variety of forms, therefore enriching our learning community.

At Public School 150, we are proud of our long-standing commitment to the arts and of our recent development of theater offerings. The arts play a significant role in daily instruction at our school. Students receive stand-alone instruction as well as arts instruction integrated into our in-depth science and social studies themes. Each year, all our work comes together in our annual arts festival, which includes a visual arts exhibit with work from every student in the school and an original theater piece that incorporates dance, music, theater and content study artwork. The theater piece is performed on the main stage of Stuyvesant High School for our families. This year it will be done virtually.

P.S. 102 The Bayview is committed to an exemplary program in the arts and credits its success to the support it receives from all stakeholders-administration, staff, parents and our rich population of up-and-coming student artists! Despite this year’s challenges, art instruction at P.S. 102 encompassed visual arts, instrumental & choral music complemented by technology arts lessons. Rich in cultural diversity our arts lessons are sensitive to the needs of all of our learners providing students with creative outlet and voice. Curriculums are aligned with NYCDOE Blue Prints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts. Though unavailable in person, these P.S. 102 highlights are alive and well in our memories  and we hope for the return next year of Art Gala, opera production, chorus performances, violin recital, STEAM Showcase, band concerts, talent show  and international celebration. These events are a testimony to the rich array of arts experiences provided to students. P.S. 102 believes that the arts are an integral part of a successful school environment and support social emotional and academic achievement. A thriving collaborative arts environment aimed at the highest level of creative achievement is a cornerstone of the P.S. 102 philosophy. Remote instruction in the arts has shifted in format, but not in content, meaning or impact. This forged new platforms for teaching and learning, enriched exposure to technology and promoted awareness that cultural arts venues from around the world are just a "click" away.

Our arts program was adapted this year to fit the needs of remote and hybrid students. Ninth, 10th, and 12th grade students were offered adapted courses that offered instruction and support in creating performing, visual, and photography arts as specific electives were not available this year due to teaching constraints.  Students created passion and skill projects within a specific art purpose and an original art series across several mediums. Students explored mixed-media drawing/painting/collage, digital photography, costume and fashion design, and photo editing to create visually and conceptually compelling works of art that fulfill aesthetic, expressive, narrative, and/or political art purposes. Students had the opportunity to engage in supplementary arts experiences through Student Learning Labs and clubs such as art, film, music, and drama. Our drama club wrote and produced several successful community-building events, including remote performances that were selected to be a part of the Shubert High School Theatre Festival. The Art Department hosted two virtual art shows and more than a dozen students were selected to be a part of the Brooklyn Borough Arts Festival. We hope to be able to continue offering rigorous and meaningful arts experiences moving forward in a greater range of media, including graphic design, music production, and film editing.

Innovation Diploma Plus (IDP) High School offers arts courses in visual arts, theater, and mixed media. Our arts courses focus on using an inter-disciplinary approach that allow students to explore connections between notions of self and community. Within that process, students present a narrative through their own use of multi-media and performance and explore critical issues that are important to them. Each course has culminating authentic assessments that function as part of a student’s ongoing portfolio. In addition to arts courses, IDP incorporates art-based instruction within the social studies and English Language Arts curriculum through the use of authentic assessments, projects and teaching artists. Teachers at IDP collaborate with outside cultural organizations, including Creative Art Works and Young Life, to offer afterschool programs in theater, visual arts, spoken word, creative writing, and video production. During the 2020-21 school year, IDP produced multiple remote theater productions, three remote art exhibits and one spoken word performance. Over the course of the school year, students had opportunities to attend cultural arts events,including the Metropolitan Museum of Art exhibitions and Broadway shows. For the 2021-22 school year, IDP will be collaborating with Creative Art Works (Artist In Resident), Studio in a School, Theatre East and Theatre Now, to create extensive art experiences for all students.

At Andries Hudde, we provided students with a robust arts program that included visual arts, band and dance. During their career at our middle school, we try to ensure that every student experiences each of the arts. Remote students received dance instruction and in-person students received band or visual arts. We had two community-based organizations working with us to compliment our arts program this year. This included Ajna Dance and Puppetry in Practice.  Both delivered their program virtually.

Our distinctive arts program offers students hands-on experiences through a variety of instructional and cultural initiatives. Our partnerships with Nalini Kids, Midori & Friends and Salvadori Center expose our students to theater, visual arts, music, and dance. Students learn a variety of artistic processes from inception to presentation. We celebrate the arts throughout the year through shows, exhibits and classroom presentations attended by students, staff, and family members. Arts is an integral part of our curriculum, and we are dedicated to creating lifelong learners and advocates for the arts.

Fannie Lou Hammer Middle School’s (FLHMS) arts program is comprised of artistic experiences at all grade levels in both the visual and performing arts. Our goal is to expose students to a variety of arts disciplines and experiences as a point of entry for a variety of student learners. Our program includes a full-time visual art teacher offering weekly lessons in both two and three dimensional art that include drawing studies, drawing techniques, sculpture, fiber arts, and graphic design projects across all three grade levels. We also have a full-time theater teacher and partner with Broadway Bound Kids and Broadway Jr. to put on a musical in the spring. This year we increased art-based offerings by incorporating dance and music instruction at all grade levels for the entire year through our afterschool program. After school, we have a FLHMS Dance Squad. This has also created opportunity for student self-expression in culminating performing arts showcases. We also have arts-based curricula that is integrated into subjects across the content areas. As a summation of our arts program, our annual schoolwide celebration, the Community School Forum, featured an explicit arts-based theme that engaged students, families and community members in student performances, mural making, gallery walk, and live art expo.

q42_1_rev: The Maure Magnet School is a growing community that provides a warm, welcoming climate and culture for all stakeholders. It has a school-based focus on communication arts, technology and multi-media to create global citizens for the future. Students are engaged in the various modalities and forms of the arts through project-based units in all grades across multi-subject areas. Student art forms are illuminated within the school and virtually through visual arts displays, music, dance, and plays. They are publicized and viewed on our school-wide social media platforms for all stakeholders. This year due to the pandemic, to better support and address different aspects of social emotional learning (SEL) in everyday practice in blended and remote learning either through individual or across multiple competencies (self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship skills, and responsible decision making) are being addressed in a tacit way, making explicit connections to the visual and performing arts through standards to better support the on-going learning and curriculum in grade-level Project-Based Learning (PBL) units and utilizing many teaching artists that perform and share their crafts. We collaborate with community based organizations for art residencies in-house and whole school virtually and virtual field trips. Students can then make clear connections to visual arts concepts and generate a strong understanding of the ‘big ideas’ to solve real world problems.

The mission of the Baychester Middle School Theatre Department is an all-inclusive program that inspires its participants and audiences to appreciate and understand the arts through quality live productions and educational opportunities. Studies have shown that students with sustained involvement in theater show substantial improvement in reading-proficiency, self-concept and motivation, and higher levels of empathy for others. At Baychester, we have witnessed first-hand the confidence that is built, the friendships that are formed, and the passions that are developed within our program. For the past two years, all sixth grade students have participated in a daily 50-minute theater course in which they learn about playwriting, design (costume, set, makeup), acting and directing basics, history of theater, script analysis, and more. There is one Blackbox production each fall and any sixth, seventh, or eighth grader may audition. There is one large-scale musical each spring for which any student in the school may audition.

The College Academy (TCA) elevates students creatively and intellectually to express their ideas in visual form to perceive not only historical contexts, but how it relates to the dynamics of culture in community based art. The College Academy’s visual arts courses range from art foundations, intermediate level AP Prep as well as Advanced Placement Studio Art. In Art Foundations, students learn how to apply the Elements of Art and Principles of Design in basic level drawing and design skills from a large scope of art genres. In Intermediate Art, students are encouraged to use symbolic themes within their work to create deeper meaning. In Advanced Art, the goal is for students to develop their own artistic voice and prepare them to work professionally for the future study of art after high school. Students of all grade levels celebrate their work with two large art shows in the winter and spring. Our photography class covers the use of Digital DSLR camera controls, including f/stops, shutter speeds, film speeds and the production of a correct exposure. Students learn composition, criticism, lighting and the history and invention of photography. This includes, exposure triangle and creative use of the camera controls, including depth of field, action motion, shadows and light, portraits, still lifes, and compositions based on the principles and elements of design. It is our ultimate goal at TCA to celebrate and provide a platform of growth through visual arts for all students.

P.S./I.S. 66 offers alternative types of arts programs that align with the New York City Blueprints for Teaching and Learning in the Arts and the Common Core Standards. At our school, we provide learning through STEAM, cooking, visual arts, music and many more art outlets for our students to grow. Our goal is to provide exposure to the arts in the elementary grades and develop a comprehensive sequential arts program for middle school by not only focusing on 2-D and 3-D design, but exploring the arts through other outlets. Pre-kindergarten through fifth grade are being immersed in the culture of peer learning through STEAM education. Lessons such as step-by-step recipes, team cooking, team- building skills, creation, and more are happening within our classrooms everyday. Cooking Threads has been very helpful to facilitate the cooking program. Students have been accepted into art shows and music students perform at nursing homes as part of community outreach. Visual arts and music teachers collaborate with classroom teachers to provide cross-curricular learning. Eight classrooms have been selected specifically to work with the STEAM cooking program, Cooking Threads, in order to provide more visual hands-on learning for our students.  Many students have submitted applications for arts programs in high schools and have been accepted.

Students are exposed to the arts in a variety of ways at PS/MS 3. They regularly participate in developmentally appropriate arts instruction in areas, including dance, music, theater, and visual arts. We have a full-time visual arts teacher that teaches students in grades K-8. Our Pre-K through 5th grade students receive additional instruction and support in music through Education Through Music. Additionally, our 6th through 8th grade students receive instruction and support in the arts through SOBRO, our community based organization. We look forward to increasing student participation in the arts for the 2021-2022 school year by expanding our relationship with Education Through Music and SOBRO sharing resources with neighboring schools and exploring virtual experiences in the arts.
Arts enrichment is provided by cultural organizations and industry professionals.  Courses include Visual Arts and Yearbook Design/Digital Media.
